docs.title: Marvin CLI Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official command-line interface for Marvin CMS. The Marvin CLI provides a powerful, flexible way to interact with your Marvin content from the terminal, scripts, and CI/CD pipelines.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 📊 Table Output by Default - Beautiful, human-readable tables in your terminal
  • 🔄 Multiple Output Formats - Choose from table, JSON, YAML, or CSV
  • 🔍 Filter and Query - Filter by entry type, collection, asset type, and more
  • 🚀 Fast - Direct HTTP calls to Marvin Publishing and Platform APIs
  • 🔐 Flexible Authentication - Site client tokens for publishing, user tokens for platform operations
  • 👥 Complete API Coverage - Access publishing, platform, and admin APIs
  • 🤖 Automation Ready - Perfect for scripts, CI/CD, and data pipelines

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install
npm install -g @inneropen/marvin-cli

# Configure
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://your-marvin-instance.com
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

# Get published entries
marvin publish entries

# Export to JSON
marvin publish entries --json > entries.json

docs.title: For Development
docs.text:
Quickly inspect content, test queries, and verify publishing workflows during development.

# Check what's published
marvin publish entries --entry-type page

# Verify a collection
marvin publish collection featured

docs.title: For Automation
docs.text:
Build automated workflows for content reporting, backups, and data processing.

# Daily content report
marvin publish entries --json | jq '.[] | select(.status == "published") | .title'

# Export all collections
marvin publish collections --csv > collections-$(date +%Y%m%d).csv

docs.title: For CI/CD
docs.text:
Integrate content validation and deployment verification into your pipelines.

# Verify deployment
if marvin publish entry homepage --json > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "✓ Homepage published"
else
  echo "✗ Homepage not found"
  exit 1
fi

docs.title: Contributing to Marvin CLI
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to the Marvin CLI! This guide will help you get started.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive environment. Please be respectful and professional in all interactions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js 18 or higher
  • npm or yarn
  • A Marvin instance for testing
  • Git

docs.title: Find Something to Work On
docs.text:
• Check the issues page
  • Look for issues labeled good first issue or help wanted
  • Or propose a new feature by opening an issue first

docs.title: 1. Fork and Clone
docs.text:
# Fork the repository on GitHub
# Then clone your fork
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/marvin-cli.git
cd marvin-cli

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text: npm install

docs.title: 3. Set Up Environment
docs.text:
# Copy example environment
cp .env.example .env

# Edit with your Marvin instance details
nano .env

Example .env:

MARVIN_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=test-workspace
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_test_token

docs.title: 4. Build the CLI
docs.text: npm run build

docs.title: 5. Link for Development
docs.text:
npm link

Now you can run marvin from anywhere and it will use your local development version.

docs.title: 6. Verify Setup
docs.text:
marvin --version
marvin publish site

docs.title: Create a Branch
docs.text:
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
# or
git checkout -b fix/issue-description

Branch naming conventions: - feature/ - New features - fix/ - Bug fixes - docs/ - Documentation changes - refactor/ - Code refactoring - test/ - Test additions or changes

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
We follow standard TypeScript conventions:

  • Use TypeScript for all new code
  • Run ESLint: npm run lint
  • Format with Prettier (if configured)
  • Use meaningful variable names
  • Add comments for complex logic
  • Keep functions small and focused

docs.text:

├── src/
│   ├── commands/        # Command implementations

docs.title: Adding a New Command
docs.text:
1. Create command file in appropriate directory:
// src/commands/publish/example.ts
import { Command } from "commander";
import { getPublishClient } from "../../shared/client.js";
import { formatOutput } from "../../output.js";

export function registerExampleCommands(program: Command) {
  program
    .command("example")
    .description("Example command description")
    .option("--limit <number>", "Limit results", "20")
    .action(async (options) => {
      const client = getPublishClient();
      const data = await client.fetchExample();
      formatOutput(data, options);
    });
}
  1. Register in parent command:
// src/commands/publish/index.ts
import { registerExampleCommands } from "./example.js";

export function createPublishCommand(): Command {
  const publish = new Command("publish");

  registerExampleCommands(publish);
  // ... other commands

  return publish;
}
  1. Add tests (when test suite exists):
// tests/commands/example.test.ts
describe("example command", () => {
  it("should fetch example data", async () => {
    // Test implementation
  });
});

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
# Make changes
code src/commands/publish/example.ts

# Build
npm run build

# Test manually
marvin publish example

# Or use watch mode
npm run dev

# In another terminal
marvin publish example

docs.title: Manual Testing
docs.text:
# Test your changes
marvin publish entries
marvin publish entry homepage --json
marvin --api-url https://staging.example.com publish site

# Test error handling
marvin publish entry nonexistent
marvin --api-url http://invalid publish site

# Test different output formats
marvin publish entries --json
marvin publish entries --yaml
marvin publish entries --csv

docs.title: Test Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Command works with default options
  • [ ] All flags work as expected
  • [ ] JSON output is valid
  • [ ] YAML output is valid
  • [ ] CSV output is valid
  • [ ] Error handling works
  • [ ] Help text is clear
  • [ ] Examples in help are correct

docs.title: 1. Commit Your Changes
docs.text:
Follow Conventional Commits:

# Feature
git commit -m "feat: add export command for bulk data export"

# Bug fix
git commit -m "fix: handle null values in CSV output"

# Documentation
git commit -m "docs: add examples for filtering entries"

# Refactor
git commit -m "refactor: extract output formatting to shared module"

Commit types: - feat: - New feature - fix: - Bug fix - docs: - Documentation changes - style: - Code style changes (formatting) - refactor: - Code refactoring - test: - Adding or updating tests - chore: - Maintenance tasks

docs.title: 2. Push to Your Fork
docs.text: git push origin feature/your-feature-name

docs.title: 3. Create Pull Request
docs.text:
1. Go to the main repository
  2. Click "Pull Requests" → "New Pull Request"
  3. Click "compare across forks"
  4. Select your fork and branch
  5. Fill out the PR template

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: Releases are automated using semantic-release.

docs.title: Version Numbers
docs.text:
We follow Semantic Versioning:

  • Major (1.0.0): Breaking changes
  • Minor (0.1.0): New features (backwards compatible)
  • Patch (0.0.1): Bug fixes

docs.title: Release Steps
docs.text:
1. Merge PR to main branch
  2. semantic-release runs automatically
  3. Version bumped based on commit messages
  4. Changelog generated
  5. npm package published
  6. GitHub release created

docs.title: What Triggers Releases
docs.text:
Based on commit messages:

  • feat: → Minor version bump
  • fix: → Patch version bump
  • feat!: or BREAKING CHANGE: → Major version bump

docs.title: Admin Backups
docs.text: Server-side backups of workspaces: list the backups on the server, download one, create a backup for a workspace and import backup data into a workspace. For the current workspace's own export and backup commands see Workspaces.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin admin backups list
marvin admin backups download <filename> [-o, --out-file <path>]
marvin admin backups create <workspace-id>
marvin admin backups import <workspace-id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)

Required role

Every marvin admin command needs the SUPER_ADMIN platform role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403).

docs.title: List
docs.text:
marvin admin backups list

Columns: filename, size, createdAt.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
marvin admin backups list
marvin admin backups download acme-20261014 --out-file ./acme-backup
Option Description Default -o, --out-file <path> Write the backup content to a file print to stdout

Use a filename exactly as list shows it. Without -o the content is printed to stdout in the selected output format; with -o the command writes the file and prints Backup written to <path>.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
marvin admin backups create 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25

Creates a backup of the given workspace (by id) on the server and prints the result. It shows up in list afterwards.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
marvin admin backups import 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 --file ./backup.json
cat backup.json | marvin admin backups import 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 --data -
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Backup data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the backup data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none

Imports the backup data into the target workspace and prints Imported backup into workspace <id> (and any details the server returns); with --json the result is {"ok": true, ...}. There is no confirmation prompt, so check the target workspace id first.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Workspaces - workspace export and workspace backups for the active workspace
  • Admin groups & workspace members - find workspace ids with admin groups list

docs.title: Admin Email
docs.text: Platform-level email: view the server's SMTP settings, send a test message through them, and manage the system email templates. Workspace-specific templates and subscriptions are covered in Email and Email Templates.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin admin email settings
marvin admin email test <email>
marvin admin email templates list
marvin admin email templates get <id>
marvin admin email templates create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin email templates update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin email templates test <id> <email>
marvin admin email templates delete <id> --yes

Required role

Every marvin admin command needs the SUPER_ADMIN platform role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403).

docs.title: Settings and test
docs.text:
marvin admin email settings
marvin admin email test admin@example.com

settings shows the SMTP configuration the server uses (host, port, username, from address and whether TLS is on). The password is never returned, and there is no command to change the settings. test sends a test message to <email> through the configured SMTP server and prints Test email sent to <email>, or {"ok": true, "email": "<email>"} with --json. A delivery failure comes back as an error from the server.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: System templates are the platform-wide email templates, as opposed to a workspace's own.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin admin email templates list
marvin admin email templates get 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93

list columns: id, name, templateType, enabled, groupId. get adds description, subject, bodyMarkdown, customHtml, availableVariables and the created / updated timestamps.

docs.title: Create and update
docs.text:
marvin admin email templates create --data '{
  "templateType": "welcome",
  "name": "Welcome",
  "subject": "Welcome to Marvin",
  "bodyMarkdown": "Your account is ready.",
  "enabled": true
}'

marvin admin email templates update 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --data '{"enabled": false}'
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Template data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the template data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none

create requires templateType, name, subject and enabled; description, bodyMarkdown, customHtml, availableVariables and groupId are optional. update takes any of name, description, subject, bodyMarkdown, customHtml, availableVariables and enabled (the type and group cannot be changed). Both print Created email template: <id> / Updated email template: <id> and then the template.

docs.title: Test and delete
docs.text:
marvin admin email templates test 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 admin@example.com
marvin admin email templates delete 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --yes

test sends the template to <email> and prints Test email for template <id> sent to <email> ({"ok": true, "templateId": ..., "email": ...} with --json). delete needs --yes; without it the command exits 1 without calling the API. With --json the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Email - workspace SMTP test and event subscriptions
  • Email Templates - templates for a single workspace

docs.title: Admin Groups & Workspace Members
docs.text: "Group" is the platform's name for a workspace. These commands create, inspect, rename and delete workspaces across the whole platform, and manage who belongs to them, whichever workspace you are currently in. Members of your active workspace are managed with marvin platform workspace-members, which needs only the workspace ADMIN role.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin admin groups list [--page <number>] [--per-page <number>] [--all]
marvin admin groups create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin groups get <id>
marvin admin groups update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin groups delete <id> --yes [--force] [--confirm-name <name>] [--skip-backup]

marvin admin workspace-members list <workspace-id>
marvin admin workspace-members get <workspace-id> <user-id>
marvin admin workspace-members add <workspace-id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin workspace-members update-role <workspace-id> <user-id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin workspace-members remove <workspace-id> <user-id> --yes

Required role

Every marvin admin command needs the SUPER_ADMIN platform role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403). Member roles are the workspace roles: OWNER, ADMIN, EDITOR, AUTHOR and VIEWER.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
marvin admin groups list
marvin admin groups list --all --json | jq -r '.[].slug'
Option Description Default --page <number> Page number 1 --per-page <number> Items per page 50 --all Fetch every page (ignores --page) off

Columns: id, name, slug.

docs.title: Create, get, update
docs.text:
marvin admin groups create --data '{"name": "Acme Studio"}'
marvin admin groups get 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25
marvin admin groups update 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 \
  --data '{"id": "5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25", "name": "Acme Studios"}'
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Group data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the group data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none

create needs a name. get prints the workspace: id, name, slug, its users, preferences and webhooks. update sends the group-admin schema, which has name and id (both required by the API schema) and optional preferences. create and update print Created group: <id> / Updated group: <id> and then the group.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin admin groups delete 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 --yes
marvin admin groups delete 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 --yes --force
marvin admin groups delete 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 --yes --skip-backup
marvin admin groups delete 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 --yes --confirm-name "Marketing"
Option Description Default --yes Confirm the deletion (required) off --force Delete even if the group has members or content off --confirm-name <name> The workspace's name, sent to the server as confirmation the workspace's own name, looked up from <id> --skip-backup Delete without a recent backup off

The server checks two things before it deletes a workspace:

  • Name confirmation. The request must carry the workspace's name. --yes is your confirmation, so by default the CLI fetches the workspace and sends its name. Pass --confirm-name to send a name you type yourself; if it doesn't match the server refuses with 400 confirm_name_mismatch.
  • A recent backup. A backup bundle of the workspace from the last 24 hours must exist, otherwise the server refuses with 409 backup_required. The CLI then tells you to run marvin admin backups create <id> (see Admin Backups) or to repeat the delete with --skip-backup.

Without --yes the command exits 1 without calling the API. Without --force the server may refuse to delete a group that still has members or content. With --json the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Workspace members
docs.text:
<workspace-id> is the group id from admin groups list; <user-id> is the id from admin users list.

marvin admin workspace-members list 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25
marvin admin workspace-members get 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10

list columns: id, userId, groupId, workspaceRole. get prints one membership, including the user summary (username, email, fullName).

docs.title: Add, change role, remove
docs.text:
marvin admin workspace-members add 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 \
  --data '{"userId": "3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10", "workspaceRole": "EDITOR"}'

marvin admin workspace-members update-role 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10 \
  --data '{"workspaceRole": "ADMIN"}'

marvin admin workspace-members remove 5b0e8c14-2d7f-4a36-b9d1-6e3f0a7c8d25 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10 --yes
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Member data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin (add, update-role) none --file <path> JSON file with the member data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none --yes Confirm the removal (remove; required) off

add takes userId and workspaceRole; update-role takes workspaceRole. Both print a confirmation and the membership. remove without --yes exits 1 without calling the API; with --json it returns {"deleted": "<user-id>"}.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Admin users - accounts and platform roles
  • Workspace members - platform workspace-members for the active workspace

docs.title: Maintenance & Scheduled Tasks
docs.text: Storage and statistics for the Marvin server, and the system-wide scheduled tasks that do its housekeeping. Cleanup is no longer a set of maintenance commands: it runs as scheduled tasks, which you can also trigger by hand with marvin admin scheduled-tasks run.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin admin maintenance summary
marvin admin maintenance stats
marvin admin maintenance storage

marvin admin scheduled-tasks list
marvin admin scheduled-tasks log [--limit <n>]
marvin admin scheduled-tasks types
marvin admin scheduled-tasks get <id>
marvin admin scheduled-tasks run <id-or-slug>
marvin admin scheduled-tasks history <id> [--limit <n>]
marvin admin scheduled-tasks create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin scheduled-tasks update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin scheduled-tasks delete <id> --yes

Required role

Every marvin admin command needs the SUPER_ADMIN platform role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403). Tasks that belong to a single workspace are managed with marvin platform scheduled-tasks and need the workspace ADMIN role instead.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
These three commands only read; none takes options beyond the global options.

marvin admin maintenance summary   # dataDirSize: size of the data directory
marvin admin maintenance storage   # tempDirSize, backupsDirSize, seedsDirSize, pluginDirSize
marvin admin maintenance stats     # maintenance statistics as reported by the server

marvin admin maintenance storage --json | jq -r '.tempDirSize'

Sizes are strings as formatted by the server. The old maintenance clean-temp, cleanup, clear-cache and optimize commands are gone; use the scheduled tasks below.

docs.title: Scheduled tasks
docs.text: System scheduled tasks span all workspaces. Each has an id (UUID), a slug, a taskType, a schedule (scheduleType of cron, interval or once, plus scheduleConfig) and a taskConfig.

docs.title: List, types and get
docs.text:
marvin admin scheduled-tasks list
marvin admin scheduled-tasks types
marvin admin scheduled-tasks get 7d1b6a52-0c3e-4f1a-8a47-92e0d5c4b3f1

list columns: id, name, slug, taskType, enabled, lastStatus, nextRunAt. types lists the available task types (task type, name, description) that create accepts. get takes the task id and prints the full record: schedule and task config, retryPolicy, lastRunAt, lastDurationMs, failureCount and timestamps.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
marvin admin scheduled-tasks run cleanup_temp_files
marvin admin scheduled-tasks run optimize_database
marvin admin scheduled-tasks run 7d1b6a52-0c3e-4f1a-8a47-92e0d5c4b3f1

Triggers one execution now. The argument is the task id or its slug; a slug is looked up in list and must match exactly one task, otherwise the command fails and asks you to use the id. Prints Executed task <id-or-slug>, or {"ok": true, "taskId": "<id>"} with --json. Read the outcome with history.

docs.title: Log and history
docs.text:
marvin admin scheduled-tasks log --limit 20
marvin admin scheduled-tasks history 7d1b6a52-0c3e-4f1a-8a47-92e0d5c4b3f1 --limit 5
Option Description Default --limit <n> Maximum number of entries server default

log is the execution log across all tasks; history is the same for one task (by id). Columns: id, taskId, status, executedAt, durationMs, errorMessage.

docs.title: Create and update
docs.text:
marvin admin scheduled-tasks create --data '{
  "name": "Weekly temp cleanup",
  "taskType": "cleanup_temp_files",
  "scheduleType": "cron",
  "scheduleConfig": {"cron_expression": "0 2 * * 0"},
  "taskConfig": {"age_hours": 24},
  "enabled": true
}'

marvin admin scheduled-tasks update 7d1b6a52-0c3e-4f1a-8a47-92e0d5c4b3f1 --data '{"enabled": false}'
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Task data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the task data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none

create takes name, taskType (see types), scheduleType, scheduleConfig and enabled, and optionally slug, description, taskConfig and retryPolicy. update takes any of name, description, enabled, scheduleType, scheduleConfig, taskConfig and retryPolicy; it does not accept slug or taskType. Unlike platform scheduled-tasks update, there are no --enable / --disable flags: set enabled in the payload.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin admin scheduled-tasks delete 7d1b6a52-0c3e-4f1a-8a47-92e0d5c4b3f1 --yes

--yes is required; without it the command exits 1 without calling the API. With --json the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Admin system - server info, counts and plugins
  • Workspace scheduled tasks - tasks scoped to one workspace

docs.title: Admin System
docs.text: Read-only information about the Marvin server: version and configuration, record counts, startup settings, a health check and the installed plugin packages.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin admin system info
marvin admin system stats
marvin admin system startup-info
marvin admin system health
marvin admin system plugins

None of them take options beyond the global options.

Required role

Every marvin admin command needs the SUPER_ADMIN platform role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403). For an unauthenticated reachability check use marvin system health.

docs.title: Info
docs.text:
marvin admin system info
marvin admin system info --json | jq -r '.version, .versionLatest'

Server details as a key/value listing: version and versionLatest, buildId, production, demoStatus, apiPort, apiDocs, dbType (and dbUrl when the server returns it), allowSignup, defaultGroup / defaultGroupSlug, and the sign-in and AI switches enableOidc, oidcRedirect, oidcProviderName, enableOpenai and enableOpenaiImageServices.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
marvin admin system stats

Record counts across the whole platform: users, workspaces, entries, collections, resources and assets.

docs.title: Startup info
docs.text:
marvin admin system startup-info

The configuration the server started with, as a key/value listing (for example the version, API port, database provider, default group and whether sign-up is allowed). Which keys appear depends on the server version.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
marvin admin system health

Asks the server for its status and prints System status: <status> in table mode, or {"status": "..."} with --json.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
marvin admin system plugins

Lists the installed plugin packages, whether each one loaded, and the integration and AI providers it adds. Columns: Name, Kind, Version, Loaded (yes, or no: <error> when the plugin failed to load) and Providers (<slug> (<n> ws): the provider and how many workspaces use it).

marvin admin system plugins --json | jq '.[] | select(.ok == false) | {name, error}'

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Maintenance & scheduled tasks - storage figures and housekeeping runs
  • Health & version - marvin system health and marvin system version

docs.title: Admin Users
docs.text: Platform-wide user management: list, create, change and delete accounts, issue password reset tokens and unlock accounts that were locked after failed sign-ins.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin admin users list [--page <number>] [--per-page <number>]
marvin admin users get <id>
marvin admin users create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin users update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin admin users delete <id> --yes
marvin admin users reset-password <user-id>
marvin admin users unlock <user-id>

Required role

Every marvin admin command needs the SUPER_ADMIN platform role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403). This is a platform role, separate from the workspace roles.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
marvin admin users list
marvin admin users list --page 2 --per-page 100
Option Description Default --page <number> Page number 1 --per-page <number> Items per page 50

Columns: id, username, fullName, email, platformRole. One page is returned per call; there is no --all, so step --page until a page comes back empty.

marvin admin users list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.platformRole == "SUPER_ADMIN") | .email'

docs.title: Get
docs.text:
marvin admin users get 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10

Prints the full user record. Fields include id, username, fullName, email, authMethod (MARVIN, LDAP or OIDC), platformRole (NONE or SUPER_ADMIN), group / groupId / groupSlug, activeGroupId, the admin, advanced, canInvite, canManage and canOrganize flags, and workspaceMemberships.

docs.title: Create and update
docs.text:
marvin admin users create --data '{
  "email": "sam@example.com",
  "username": "sam",
  "fullName": "Sam Rivera",
  "authMethod": "MARVIN",
  "platformRole": "NONE",
  "password": "<initial-password>"
}'

marvin admin users update 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10 --data '{"platformRole": "SUPER_ADMIN"}'
marvin admin users update 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10 --file ./user-patch.json
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> User data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the user data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none

create requires email, authMethod, platformRole and password; username, fullName and the permission flags are optional. update takes any of username, fullName, email, authMethod and platformRole. Both print Created user: <id> / Updated user: <id> on stderr and then the user.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin admin users delete 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10 --yes

--yes is required: without it the command prints an error and exits 1 without calling the API. With --json the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Reset password
docs.text:
marvin admin users reset-password 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10

Generates a password reset token for the user and prints it with the path the user opens to finish the reset (/reset-password?token=...). The token is shown in full only in an interactive terminal; when stdout is not a TTY (CI, a pipe, a log) it is masked and a warning is written to stderr, so run this command interactively. With --json or --yaml the output is { userId, token, resetPath }. Treat the token as a credential and send it to the user over a private channel.

docs.title: Unlock
docs.text:
marvin admin users unlock 3f2c9d1e-7a54-4b0e-9c1a-5d8e2f6b7a10

Clears the lock on an account. Prints User <id> unlocked successfully, or {"ok": true, "userId": "<id>"} with --json.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Admin groups & workspace members - which workspaces a user belongs to
  • User account - what a user can change about themselves

docs.title: AI
docs.text: marvin platform ai manages the workspace's AI setup: provider connections and their models, the catalogue of AI operations (and running them), the execution audit log, and the workspace AI settings. All commands use the Platform API, so they need a user login or MARVIN_USER_TOKEN (see Authentication).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform ai providers list
marvin platform ai providers get <id>
marvin platform ai providers create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform ai providers update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform ai providers delete <id> --yes
marvin platform ai providers test <id>

marvin platform ai providers models list <provider-id>
marvin platform ai providers models create <provider-id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform ai providers models update <provider-id> <model-id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform ai providers models delete <provider-id> <model-id> --yes

marvin platform ai operations list
marvin platform ai operations get <slug>
marvin platform ai operations execute <slug> [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>]
marvin platform ai operations reindex [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>]

marvin platform ai executions list [--operation-slug <slug>] [--status <status>] [--entity-id <id>] [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>]
marvin platform ai executions get <id>
marvin platform ai executions delete <id> --yes

marvin platform ai settings show
marvin platform ai settings update (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)

There is no shorter alias for ai; it only exists under platform.

Required role

Everything under providers, including its models, needs ADMIN (or OWNER), reads included. The other groups have no role gate in the CLI. The backend decides: each operation carries a minimum role (min_role in operations get), and the SDK documents that settings writes need ADMIN/OWNER. A 403 is reported with the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

Write commands take a JSON body from --data <json|@file|-> (inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin), from --file <path>, or from piped stdin. The body must be a JSON object, with camelCase keys. delete commands refuse to run without --yes.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: A provider is a connection to an LLM service. providerType is one of openai, anthropic, google, azure, ollama or custom.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform ai providers list
marvin platform ai providers get 3d9c…

list columns: ID, Name, Slug, Provider Type, Enabled, Is Default. get prints the full provider, including its models.

docs.title: Create and update
docs.text:
create requires name, slug and providerType. Optional: baseUrl, enabled, isDefault, metadataJson and secretRef. update takes the same keys, all optional, and changes only the ones you send.

marvin platform ai providers create --data '{
  "name": "Anthropic",
  "slug": "anthropic",
  "providerType": "anthropic",
  "secretRef": "<secret-reference>",
  "enabled": true,
  "isDefault": true
}'

marvin platform ai providers update 3d9c… --data '{"enabled": false}'

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: A provider never holds an API key in its own fields. secretRef points at a workspace secret, and the key itself lives in the secret store (Secrets and variables). The CLI has no key flag, so a key does not end up in your shell history through this command, and get/list show only the reference. Create the secret first, then put its reference in secretRef. Read bodies from a file or stdin when they hold anything you would not paste into a terminal.

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
marvin platform ai providers test 3d9c…

Checks the provider's credentials and connection. The result has success, a message and availableModels (the model ids the provider reports). Run it after creating a provider or rotating its secret.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin platform ai providers delete 3d9c… --yes

With --json, prints {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Models are the specific model ids a provider offers, and are managed under their provider.

marvin platform ai providers models list 3d9c…
marvin platform ai providers models create 3d9c… --data '{
  "name": "Claude Sonnet",
  "modelId": "claude-sonnet-4-5",
  "isDefault": true,
  "supportsTools": true,
  "supportsVision": true
}'
marvin platform ai providers models update 3d9c… 8b21… --data '{"enabled": false}'
marvin platform ai providers models delete 3d9c… 8b21… --yes

list columns: ID, Name, Model Id, Is Default, Enabled. create requires name and modelId; optional keys are isDefault, enabled, contextWindow, maxOutputTokens, supportsVision and supportsTools. update takes the same keys, all optional. <model-id> in update and delete is the model's record id (the id column), not its modelId.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Operations are the built-in AI tasks the backend offers (summaries, tag suggestions, alt text and so on).

marvin platform ai operations list
marvin platform ai operations get generate-summary

list columns: Slug, Name, Description. get also returns the operation's input_schema and output_schema, entity_types it applies to, min_role, and requires_vision. Read the input schema before building an execute body.

docs.title: Execute
docs.text:
marvin platform ai operations execute <slug> [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>]
Body key Description entityType Type of the entity the operation runs against (see entity_types on the operation) entityId Id of that entity input Operation-specific input object, shaped by the operation's input_schema modelOverride Use this model for the call instead of the workspace default source Invocation surface; normally set by the calling infrastructure, and checked against the workspace's AI policy

All keys are optional. With no --data/--file and an interactive terminal, the CLI sends an empty body {}. When stdin is not a terminal (a script, CI), it reads the body from stdin instead, so pass --data '{}' explicitly there.

marvin platform ai operations execute generate-summary \
  --data '{"entityType": "entry", "entityId": "6f1c…"}'

Execution is synchronous. The command returns the finished execution record, which is also written to the audit log: status (completed or failed), outputJson (the operation's result), errorMessage, operationSlug, providerType, modelId, token counts (promptTokens, completionTokens, totalTokens), estimatedCostUsd, durationMs and timestamps. Pull out just the result with:

marvin platform ai operations execute generate-tags --file body.json --json | jq '.outputJson'

docs.title: Reindex
docs.text:
marvin platform ai operations reindex [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>]

Rebuilds the RAG embeddings index over the workspace's published content. The optional body can narrow the work: entityType, entityId, scope, and force (default false). An empty body reindexes everything the backend would normally cover.

marvin platform ai operations reindex
marvin platform ai operations reindex --data '{"entityType": "entry", "force": true}'

With --json the result is {"ok": true, …} plus whatever the backend returns.

docs.title: Executions
docs.text:
Every operation run is recorded in the audit log, newest first.

marvin platform ai executions list --operation-slug generate-summary --status failed --limit 20
marvin platform ai executions get 5e0a…
marvin platform ai executions delete 5e0a… --yes
Option Description Default --operation-slug <slug> Only runs of this operation all --status <status> Only runs in this status (pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled) all --entity-id <id> Only runs against this entity all --limit <number> Maximum number of results not sent --offset <number> Number of results to skip not sent

list columns: ID, Operation Slug, Status, Entity Type, Entity Id, Created At. get prints the full record, including outputJson and errorMessage. delete removes the audit record only.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Workspace-wide AI policy.

marvin platform ai settings show
marvin platform ai settings update --data '{"enabled": true, "approvalMode": "suggest-only"}'

show returns the current settings (defaults if none were saved yet). update upserts: send only the keys you want to change.

Key Description enabled Master switch for AI in this workspace credentialMode platform, workspace or disabled provider, model Default provider and model secretRef Reference to the secret holding the workspace's credential (a reference, not a key) approvalMode suggest-only, allow-draft-update or allow-automatic-update invocationSources, operationOverrides, budgetConfig, loggingConfig, moderationConfig Policy objects externalMcpEnabled Whether the agent may use tools from registered external MCP servers assistantName, personaPrompt, defaultRegister Assistant persona: display name, voice/tone prompt, tone register (auto, professional, playful)

docs.title: API Clients
docs.text: An API client is a named token for the Publishing API (marvin publish ...). Each workspace can have several, for example one per site or environment. These commands create them, edit them, and rotate their tokens.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform api-clients list
marvin platform api-clients get <id>
marvin platform api-clients create (--name <name> [--description <text>] | --data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform api-clients update <id> (--name <name> | --description <text> | --data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform api-clients delete <id> --yes
marvin platform api-clients rotate-token <id>
marvin platform api-clients preview <id>

Required role

Every API client command, reads included, needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

<id> is the client's UUID (the ID column of list).

docs.title: List, get, preview
docs.text:
marvin platform api-clients list
marvin platform api-clients get 7c1e5d3a-2b9f-4e0a-8d64-5f3a9b1c0e22
marvin platform api-clients preview 7c1e5d3a-2b9f-4e0a-8d64-5f3a9b1c0e22

list columns: ID, Name, Description (first 50 characters), Created. get prints the full record (slug, enabled, permissions, last-used and created timestamps). preview prints the same record as the server returns it for a preview, which shows the token prefix and metadata without revealing the full token. Neither returns the token itself; that is only shown when a client is created or its token is rotated.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
marvin platform api-clients create --name "Production site" --description "Token for the live website"
marvin platform api-clients create --data '{"name": "Staging", "slug": "staging"}'
Option Description --name <name> Client name; a quick way to create without a JSON body --description <description> Client description (used with --name) --data <json\|@file\|-> Full body as inline JSON, @path, or - for stdin --file <path> Path to a JSON file (same as --data @path; - for stdin)

--data / --file win over --name. Without any of them the command exits 1 with Provide API client data via --data, --file, or --name. The body accepts name (required), slug, description and permissions.

The response includes the client's token, shown once. It is printed on stderr as Token: <token>; when stdout is not a terminal (CI, pipes, logs) that line is masked to the first and last four characters. The record printed on stdout (--json etc.) is the server's response and includes the full token field, so capture it from there in scripts:

TOKEN=$(marvin platform api-clients create --name "CI build" --json | jq -r .token)
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN="$TOKEN"

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
marvin platform api-clients update 7c1e5d3a-2b9f-4e0a-8d64-5f3a9b1c0e22 --description "Live site, EU"
marvin platform api-clients update 7c1e5d3a-2b9f-4e0a-8d64-5f3a9b1c0e22 --data '{"enabled": false}'

--name and --description are shortcuts; --data / --file can also set permissions and enabled (set enabled to false to switch a client off without deleting it). With no option the command exits 1 with Provide API client data via --data, --file, --name, or --description. The token is not changed.

docs.title: Rotate token
docs.text:
marvin platform api-clients rotate-token 7c1e5d3a-2b9f-4e0a-8d64-5f3a9b1c0e22

Generates a new token and invalidates the old one immediately; every site or job using the old token starts failing with 401 until it is updated. The new token is shown once, as for create (New Token: ... on stderr, token in the stdout record).

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin platform api-clients delete 7c1e5d3a-2b9f-4e0a-8d64-5f3a9b1c0e22 --yes
Option Description --yes Skip confirmation prompt (required; without it the command exits 1)

With --json the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Authentication Commands
docs.text: Save and clear the tokens the CLI uses, and handle the public account flows (register, password reset). These are top-level commands, not part of a group.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin login [--user-token <token>] [--site-token <token>] [--workspace <slug>]
marvin logout [--site-token | --all]
marvin register [--email <email>] [--password <password>] [--data <json|@file|->] [--file <path>]
marvin forgot-password <email>
marvin reset-password --token <token> --password <newPassword>

There is no marvin auth ... group and no whoami command. To see who you are, use marvin user profile show (User); to see the active workspace, use marvin workspace current (Workspaces).

The CLI authenticates with tokens, not an email and password: a user token for the Platform and Admin APIs, and a per-workspace site client token for the Publishing API. Create a user token in the Marvin UI or with marvin user tokens create (User); site client tokens are managed under API clients. See also the Authentication Reference.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
Validates the token against the server, then saves it to ~/.marvin/credentials.json.

Option Description Default --user-token <token> User token for Platform access. If omitted (and MARVIN_USER_TOKEN is unset) you are prompted, with hidden input. Prompt --site-token <token> Site client token for Publishing access. Saved for the workspace given by --workspace, or the active workspace. none --workspace <slug> Workspace slug. Required when saving a site token and no workspace is active; with a user token it also becomes the active workspace. none

The API URL must be known (--api-url, MARVIN_API_URL, or a previously saved one).

  • With neither token option, login prompts for a user token.
  • With only --site-token, only the site token is validated and saved; no user-token prompt.
  • A user token given by --user-token or MARVIN_USER_TOKEN is saved alongside any site token.
  • The first saved site token also becomes the active workspace if none is set.
# Interactive: prompts for the user token
marvin login --api-url https://marvin.example.com

# Non-interactive, and select the workspace
marvin login --user-token "$MARVIN_USER_TOKEN" --workspace acme

# Publishing API only
marvin login --site-token marvin_sk_xxx --workspace acme

After a user login without --workspace, pick one with marvin workspace use <slug>.

docs.title: Logout
docs.text:
Clears saved credentials.

Option Description Default --site-token Clear only the site token of the active workspace false --all Clear everything (user token, site tokens, active workspace, API URL) false

With no option only the user token is removed and site tokens are kept.

marvin logout
marvin logout --site-token
marvin logout --all

docs.title: Register
docs.text:
Creates a user account. Public: no token is needed, only an API URL. The payload is the registration data; --email and --password override the same fields in --data / --file / piped stdin.

Option Description Default --email <email> User email none --password <password> User password none --data <json\|@file\|-> Registration data as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with registration data (same as --data @path) none

Registration data fields: username, email, full_name, password and password_confirm, plus optional group_token, group, advanced, private and seed_data.

marvin register --data '{"username":"jo","email":"jo@example.com","full_name":"Jo Doe","password":"s3cret-pass","password_confirm":"s3cret-pass"}'
marvin register --file new-user.json --email jo@example.com

On success it prints Registered user: <email> followed by the created user.

docs.title: Forgot and reset password
docs.text:
forgot-password asks the server to email a reset link. It always reports success, whether or not the address exists. reset-password sets a new password using the token from that email; both options are required.

marvin forgot-password jo@example.com
marvin reset-password --token <token-from-email> --password 'a-new-s3cret-pass'

Prefer --password from an environment variable or a prompt wrapper over typing it on a shared shell, as it is visible in shell history.

docs.title: Credential sources
docs.text: Credential Resolved from (first match wins) User token (Platform, Admin) MARVIN_USER_TOKEN, then saved credentials. There is no command-line flag for it on other commands. Site client token (Publishing) --site-token / --token on marvin publish, saved token for the workspace, then MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN API URL --api-url, MARVIN_API_URL, then saved credentials

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://marvin.example.com
export MARVIN_USER_TOKEN=...        # from your secret store
export MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=acme
marvin platform entries list

No login is needed when the environment variables are set.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Workspaces
  • User
  • Environment Variables
  • Authentication Reference

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text: Blueprints are ready-made pieces of workspace structure — collections, entry types, scheduled tasks and workflows — that Marvin ships and installed integrations contribute. Browse the catalog, then apply what you want. Applying creates what's missing and never overwrites what exists, so running it twice is safe.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform blueprints list [--kind <kind>] [--category <name>] [--source <source>] [--integration-id <id>]
marvin platform blueprints categories
marvin platform blueprints get <slug> [--source <source>]
marvin platform blueprints apply <slug> [<slug>…] [--params <json|@file|->] [--source <source>] [--integration-id <id>]
marvin platform blueprints update <slug> [--params <json|@file|->] [--source <source>]

Required role

Any member browses the catalog. apply and update change workspace structure and need the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
marvin platform blueprints list
marvin platform blueprints list --kind collection --category Media
marvin platform blueprints list --source square --integration-id 0b6f…
Option Description Default --kind <kind> Only this kind: collection, entry_type, scheduled_task, workflow, … --category <name> Only this category (see categories) --source <source> Only from this source: core, or an integration provider's slug --integration-id <id> Check per-integration blueprints against this connection

Columns: Slug, Kind, Name, Category, Source (core or an integration's provider slug), Applied (yes, yes (outdated) when the workspace has an older version, or no), Available (no: needs … when the workspace lacks something it requires), Params (? marks an optional one).

--integration-id checks per-integration blueprints against one connection, for workspaces with several connections to the same provider.

docs.title: categories
docs.text:
marvin platform blueprints categories

Lists the blueprint categories, core's first, then each integration's. No options.

docs.title: get
docs.text:
marvin platform blueprints get all-{{entry_type}} --json
marvin platform blueprints get tag-new-posts --source buttondown
Argument / option Description Default <slug> Blueprint slug --source <source> Pick the blueprint from this source when several share the slug

Prints the blueprint with its parameters (key, label, kind, required, default, help) and its payload.

docs.title: apply
docs.text:
Argument / option Description Default <slugs...> One or more blueprint slugs --params <json\|@file\|-> Parameter values: {key: value} for one blueprint, {slug: {key: value}} for several; inline JSON, @path or - for stdin --data <json\|@file\|-> Same as --params --source <source> Pick blueprints from this source when several share a slug --integration-id <id> The integration connection to apply per-integration blueprints for

One blueprint, with its parameters:

marvin platform blueprints apply recently-published
marvin platform blueprints apply 'all-{{entry_type}}' --params '{"entry_type": "post"}'

Several at once — entry types are created before the collections and tasks that use them, whatever order you list them in. --params is then keyed by blueprint slug:

marvin platform blueprints apply post 'published-{{entry_type}}' \
  --params '{"published-{{entry_type}}": {"entry_type": "post"}}'
marvin platform blueprints apply post featured --params @params.json

Table mode prints a result per blueprint (Created, Updated, Detail) and a summary on stderr, e.g. ✓ Created 1 of 2 blueprint(s); the rest were already in place. With --json, one slug prints the result object and several print an array:

{ "slug": "recently-published", "kind": "collection", "created": true, "updated": false, "detail": "", "name": "Recently published" }

A blueprint that can't be applied comes back with created: false and the reason in detail (e.g. no entry type 'post' in this workspace); the command still exits 0.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
marvin platform blueprints update tag-new-posts
marvin platform blueprints update tag-new-posts --params '{"channel": "C123"}' --source slack
Argument / option Description Default <slug> Blueprint slug of an applied workflow --params <json\|@file\|-> Parameter values as {key: value} --data <json\|@file\|-> Same as --params --source <source> Pick the blueprint from this source when several share the slug

Replaces an applied workflow's steps with what its integration declares now — what Applied: yes (outdated) asks for. Other kinds answer with updated: false and say why.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text: List and retrieve collections and their entries from your Marvin workspace.

docs.title: Get Single Collection

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Collections are curated groups of entries in Marvin. They allow you to organize content into categories like "Featured Projects", "Blog Posts", or "Case Studies". The collection commands let you list all collections, get details about a specific collection, and retrieve all entries within a collection.

docs.title: marvin publish collections
docs.text: Option Description Default --limit <number> Show at most this many collections (1 to 100) server default (20) --offset <number> Skip this many collections first 0 --json Output as JSON false --yaml Output as YAML false --csv Output as CSV false --output <format> Output format: table, json, yaml, csv table

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
List collections (the server returns 20 at a time unless you ask for more):

marvin publish collections

Page through a larger workspace, 100 at a time:

marvin publish collections --limit 100

┌───────────────────┬──────────┬─────────────────┐
│ Name              │ Slug     │ Description     │
├───────────────────┼──────────┼─────────────────┤

│ Archive           │ archived │ Older content   │
│ Blog Posts        │ blog     │ Latest articles │
└───────────────────┴──────────┴─────────────────┘

Get a single collection:

marvin publish collection featured

Output (same columns as the list; use --json to see entryCount and the nested entries):

┌───────────────────┬──────────┬───────────────┐
│ Name              │ Slug     │ Description   │
├───────────────────┼──────────┼───────────────┤
│ Featured Projects │ featured │ Our best work │
└───────────────────┴──────────┴───────────────┘

marvin publish collection-entries featured

│ Order │ Title            │ Slug     │ Type    │ Status    │ Published  │
├───────┼──────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────┼────────────┤
│ 1     │ Denim Project 01 │ denim-01 │ project │ published │ 2026-07-01 │
│ 2     │ Denim Project 02 │ denim-02 │ project │ published │ 2026-07-02 │
│ 3     │ Jacket Project   │ jacket-1 │ project │ published │ 2026-07-03 │

docs.title: Verify Collection Exists
docs.text:
Check if a collection exists before querying:

if marvin publish collection featured --json > /dev/null 2>&1; then  # exit status 1 when the slug is unknown
  echo "✓ Featured collection exists"
else
  echo "✗ Featured collection not found"
fi

docs.text:
Export all entries from a specific collection:

marvin publish collection-entries featured --json > featured-entries.json

Count entries in a collection:

marvin publish collection-entries featured --json | jq 'length'

docs.title: Bash Script
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

# Get all collections
COLLECTIONS=$(marvin publish collections --json)

# Loop through each collection
echo "$COLLECTIONS" | jq -c '.[]' | while read -r collection; do
  SLUG=$(echo "$collection" | jq -r '.slug')
  NAME=$(echo "$collection" | jq -r '.name')
  COUNT=$(marvin publish collection "$SLUG" --json | jq -r '.entryCount')

  echo "Collection: $NAME ($SLUG)"
  echo "Entries: $COUNT"
  echo "---"

  # Get entries in collection
  marvin publish collection-entries "$SLUG" --json | jq -r '.[].title' | sed 's/^/  - /'
  echo ""
done
