docs.title: Static Site Generation
docs.text:
// scripts/fetch-collections.js
const { execSync } = require('child_process');
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

// Fetch all collections
const collections = JSON.parse(
  execSync('marvin publish collections --json', { encoding: 'utf-8' })
);

// Create output directory
const outputDir = 'src/data/collections';
fs.mkdirSync(outputDir, { recursive: true });

// Save collections index
fs.writeFileSync(
  path.join(outputDir, 'index.json'),
  JSON.stringify(collections, null, 2)
);

// Fetch entries for each collection
collections.forEach(collection => {
  const entries = JSON.parse(
    execSync(`marvin publish collection-entries ${collection.slug} --json`, {
      encoding: 'utf-8'
    })
  );

  // Save collection with entries
  fs.writeFileSync(
    path.join(outputDir, `${collection.slug}.json`),
    JSON.stringify({
      ...collection,
      entries
    }, null, 2)
  );

  console.log(`Saved ${collection.name} with ${entries.length} entries`);
});

console.log(`Fetched ${collections.length} collections`);

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Requires a site client token. Set in environment:

export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

Or pass via command line:

marvin publish collections --site-token marvin_sk_your_token

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
Site client token is invalid or missing:

export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

docs.title: Unknown slug
docs.text:
The command exits with status 1 (and prints [] in JSON/YAML mode) when the collection doesn't exist:

# List all collections to verify slug
marvin publish collections --json | jq -r '.[].slug'

docs.title: Empty Collection
docs.text:
Collection exists but has no entries:

marvin publish collection-entries empty-collection --json
# Returns: []

Check entry count first:

marvin publish collection empty-collection --json | jq -r '.entryCount'

docs.title: Related Commands
docs.text:
• marvin publish entries - List all entries
  • marvin publish entries --collection <slug> - Filter entries by collection
  • marvin publish entry <slug> - Get single entry
  • marvin publish site - Get site configuration

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
These commands call (collection-entries reads the entries from the single-collection response):

GET /api/publish/{workspace}/collections
GET /api/publish/{workspace}/collections/{slug}

See API Mapping for more details.

docs.title: Email Templates
docs.text: Workspace email templates customise the emails Marvin sends. A template has a type (the kind of email it replaces or adds), a subject, and either a Markdown body (rendered in the default layout) or custom HTML. These commands manage the current workspace's templates. System-level templates and SMTP are in Email; sending an email on an event is set up with email subscriptions.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates list
marvin platform email-templates get <template-id>
marvin platform email-templates create --type <type> --name <name> --subject <subject> [options]
marvin platform email-templates update <template-id> [options]
marvin platform email-templates delete <template-id> --yes
marvin platform email-templates event-connections <group-id>
marvin platform email-templates test-send <template-id> <email>

platform templates is an alias for platform email-templates; list also answers to ls, delete to rm, and test-send to test.

Required role

Listing and reading templates is open to any workspace member. Creating, updating, deleting and test-sending templates, and event-connections, need the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. See Workspace roles.

list, get, create, update, delete and test-send all act on the current workspace (the one from --workspace or marvin workspace use).

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates list
marvin platform email-templates get 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --json

list columns: Name, Type, Enabled, Scope (workspace for the workspace's own templates, system for the built-in defaults). get prints the full template.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates create \
  --type welcome --name "Welcome" --subject "Welcome to Marvin" \
  --body "Your account is ready."
Option Description Default --type <type> Template type, for example welcome or notification (required) --name <name> Template name (required) --subject <subject> Email subject (required) --description <desc> Template description none --body <markdown> Markdown body, rendered in the default layout (sent as bodyMarkdown) none --custom-html <html> Custom HTML; overrides --body none --disabled Create the template disabled enabled

The API has no separate header, message or button fields, so use --body (or --custom-html). The variables available for a template type are shown by marvin platform email template-vars --type <type>. The created template is printed on stdout and Created email template: <name> on stderr.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates update 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --subject "Welcome!" --disable
marvin platform email-templates update 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --custom-html "$(cat welcome.html)"
Option Description --name <name> Template name --subject <subject> Email subject --description <desc> Template description --body <markdown> Markdown body, rendered in the default layout --custom-html <html> Custom HTML template (overrides --body) --enable Enable the template --disable Disable the template

Only the options you pass are sent, and an empty value is ignored, so a field cannot be cleared from the command line. The type cannot be changed.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates delete 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --yes

--yes confirms (default off); without it the command prints Delete template? Use --yes to confirm and exits 1. With --json it prints {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Event connections
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates event-connections 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358

Lists the event connections available for the workspace's email templates. <group-id> is the workspace id (shown by marvin workspace list). The result is printed as returned by the server.

docs.title: Test send
docs.text:
marvin platform email-templates test-send 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 me@example.com

Sends a test email using the template to <email>. Prints the server's message and Recipient: <email> on stderr; with --json, {"ok": true, "message": "...", "recipient": "..."}. To check the SMTP configuration itself, use marvin platform email test-smtp.

docs.title: Email
docs.text: Two groups cover the email side of a workspace: platform email handles the system-level email templates and the SMTP test, and platform email-subscriptions decides which events send which template to whom. Workspace-specific templates live in Email Templates. The admin-side email settings are under marvin admin email; see admin-email.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform email template-vars --type <type>
marvin platform email get-template <id>
marvin platform email update-template <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform email test-template <id> <email>
marvin platform email test-smtp <email>

marvin platform email-subscriptions list
marvin platform email-subscriptions get <id>
marvin platform email-subscriptions create --template-id <id> --event-type <type> [--recipient-type <type>] [--recipient-email <email>] [--recipient-field <field>]
marvin platform email-subscriptions delete <id> --yes

Required role

update-template, test-template and test-smtp, and every email-subscriptions command, reads included, need the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. template-vars and get-template carry no role requirement in the CLI. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
marvin platform email template-vars --type welcome

Shows the variables available to a template of the given type. --type <type> is required.

docs.title: SMTP and system templates
docs.text:
System templates are the built-in defaults, addressed by id (the list in Email Templates marks them with Scope system).

marvin platform email get-template 2e7d9a14-6c05-4b3f-81a8-d4f0c5b92e67
marvin platform email update-template 2e7d9a14-6c05-4b3f-81a8-d4f0c5b92e67 --data '{"subject": "Reset your Marvin password"}'
marvin platform email test-template 2e7d9a14-6c05-4b3f-81a8-d4f0c5b92e67 me@example.com
marvin platform email test-smtp me@example.com
Command What it does get-template <id> Prints a system email template update-template <id> Updates it from a JSON body: --data <json\|@file\|-> (inline JSON, @path, or - for stdin) or --file <path>. Fields: name, description, subject, bodyMarkdown, customHtml, availableVariables, enabled. Prints Updated system template: <id> on stderr and the template on stdout test-template <id> <email> Sends a test email using the system template to <email> test-smtp <email> Sends a test email to <email> to check the SMTP configuration

test-template and test-smtp print the server's message and Recipient: <email> on stderr; with --json the result is {"ok": true, "message": "...", "recipient": "..."}.

docs.title: Email subscriptions
docs.text:
A subscription sends an email template when an event happens.

marvin platform email-subscriptions list
marvin platform email-subscriptions get 6f20b8c1-3a4e-49d7-b5e2-1c9d07a8f344
marvin platform email-subscriptions create --template-id 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 --event-type entry.published
marvin platform email-subscriptions create --template-id 9b3e41d7-5c28-4a60-8f17-0d2c6e4a7b93 \
  --event-type form.submitted --recipient-type specific --recipient-email ops@example.com
marvin platform email-subscriptions delete 6f20b8c1-3a4e-49d7-b5e2-1c9d07a8f344 --yes

list columns: ID, Template ID, Event Type, Recipient Type, Enabled. get prints the full subscription.

create options:

Option Description Default --template-id <id> Email template ID (required) --event-type <type> Event type to subscribe to, for example entry.published (required) --recipient-type <type> admins, specific or event_field admins --recipient-email <email> Recipient address, for specific none --recipient-field <field> Field of the event payload holding the recipient's address, for event_field none

It prints Created email subscription: <id> on stderr and the subscription on stdout. delete requires --yes (without it the command exits 1); with --json it prints {"deleted": "<id>"}. There is no update: delete and recreate to change a subscription.

docs.title: Entries
docs.text: List and retrieve published entries from your Marvin workspace.

docs.title: List Entries
docs.text: marvin publish entries [options]

docs.title: Get Single Entry
docs.text: marvin publish entry <slug>

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Entries are the primary content type in Marvin. They represent pages, blog posts, projects, or any custom entry type you've defined. The entries command lists all published entries with optional filtering, while entry retrieves a single entry by its slug.

docs.title: marvin publish entries
docs.text: Option Description Default --entry-type <slug> Filter by entry type (e.g., page, project) All types --collection <slug> Filter by collection All entries --tag <slugs> Entries carrying any of these tag slugs (comma-separated) All entries --slug <slugs> Only these entry slugs (comma-separated) All entries --updated-since <iso> Entries updated at or after this ISO 8601 date or time (rejected if unparseable) All entries --expand <mode> full is the only accepted value: return each entry as the single-entry read (assets, resources, every membership) List items --limit <number> Limit number of results All entries --offset <number> Skip this many results 0 --json Output as JSON false --yaml Output as YAML false --csv Output as CSV false --output <format> Output format: table, json, yaml, csv table

docs.title: marvin publish entry <slug>
docs.text: Option Description Default --json Output as JSON false --yaml Output as YAML false --csv Output as CSV false --output <format> Output format: table, json, yaml, csv table

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
List all published entries:

marvin publish entries

Output:

┌───────────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────────┬────────────┐
│ Title         │ Slug     │ Type    │ Status    │ Published  │
├───────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────┼────────────┤
│ About Us      │ about    │ page    │ published │ 2026-07-01 │
│ Contact       │ contact  │ page    │ published │ 2026-07-02 │
│ Denim Project │ denim-01 │ project │ published │ 2026-07-03 │
└───────────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────────┴────────────┘

Get a single entry:

marvin publish entry about

Output (one row, same columns as the list):

┌──────────┬───────┬──────┬───────────┬────────────┐
│ Title    │ Slug  │ Type │ Status    │ Published  │
├──────────┼───────┼──────┼───────────┼────────────┤
│ About Us │ about │ page │ published │ 2026-07-01 │
└──────────┴───────┴──────┴───────────┴────────────┘

Use --json to see the full entry (content, metadata, assets, resources). An unknown slug prints an empty result rather than an error.

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
List entries as JSON:

marvin publish entries --json

[
  {
    "slug": "about",
    "title": "About Us",
    "entryType": "page",
    "status": "published",
    "publishedAt": "2026-07-01T12:00:00Z",
    "description": "Learn about our company",
    "content": {
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "content": "We are a company..."
        }
      ]
    },
    "metadata": {
      "seoTitle": "About Us - My Company",
      "seoDescription": "Learn about our company"
    }
  }
]

Get a single entry as JSON (an array with one element, or [] when the slug is unknown):

marvin publish entry about --json

[
  {
    "slug": "about",
    "title": "About Us",
    "entryType": "page",
    "status": "published",
    "publishedAt": "2026-07-01T12:00:00Z",
    "description": "Learn about our company",
    "content": {
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "content": "We are a company that builds amazing products..."
        }
      ]
    },
    "metadata": {
      "seoTitle": "About Us - My Company",
      "seoDescription": "Learn about our company"
    },
    "collections": ["featured"],
    "resources": [],
    "assets": []
  }
]

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Filter by entry type:

marvin publish entries --entry-type page
marvin publish entries --entry-type project
marvin publish entries --entry-type blog-post

Filter by collection:

marvin publish entries --collection featured
marvin publish entries --collection archived

Limit results:

marvin publish entries --limit 10
marvin publish entries --limit 5 --entry-type page

Filter by tag (any of several), by slug, or by last update:

marvin publish entries --tag news,events
marvin publish entries --slug about,contact
marvin publish entries --updated-since 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z

--updated-since makes an incremental sync cheap: remember when you last synced and ask only for what changed since.

Combine filters:

marvin publish entries --entry-type project --collection featured --limit 3

docs.title: Full entries in one call
docs.text:
--expand full returns every entry on the page in the single-entry shape (its assets with roles, its resources, every collection membership), so you don't need a marvin publish entry call per item. A server that doesn't support expand returns the usual list items.

marvin publish entries --entry-type project --expand full --json | jq '.[] | {slug, assets: [.assets[].asset.slug]}'

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description slug string Unique URL-friendly identifier title string Entry title entryType string Entry type slug (page, project, etc.) status string Publication status (published, draft) publishedAt string ISO 8601 timestamp of publication description string Entry description/summary content object Structured content blocks metadata object SEO and custom metadata collections array Collection slugs this entry belongs to resources array Resources referenced in this entry assets array Assets attached to this entry createdAt string ISO 8601 timestamp of creation updatedAt string ISO 8601 timestamp of last update

docs.title: Export All Entries
docs.text:
Export all entries to JSON for static site generation:

marvin publish entries --json > entries.json

docs.title: Count Entries by Type
docs.text:
Count how many pages exist:

marvin publish entries --entry-type page --json | jq 'length'

Output:

12

docs.title: Get Latest Entries
docs.text:
Get the 5 most recent entries:

marvin publish entries --limit 5 --json | jq -r '.[].title'

Output:

Latest Blog Post
New Project Launch
Contact Page Update
About Page
Homepage

docs.title: Check if Entry Exists
docs.text:
marvin publish entry prints an empty result ([] with --json) for an unknown slug, so test the length:

if [ "$(marvin publish entry about --json | jq 'length')" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "About page exists"
else
  echo "About page not found"
fi

docs.title: Extract Entry Content
docs.text:
Get entry content for processing:

marvin publish entry about --json | jq -r '.[0].content.blocks[0].content'

docs.title: Build Site Map
docs.text:
Generate a sitemap from all entries:

marvin publish entries --json | jq -r '.[] | "https://mysite.com/\(.slug)"'

Output:

https://mysite.com/about
https://mysite.com/contact
https://mysite.com/denim-01

docs.title: Bash Script
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

# Get all published pages
PAGES=$(marvin publish entries --entry-type page --json)

# Extract titles
echo "$PAGES" | jq -r '.[] | "\(.title) - \(.slug)"'

# Count total pages
COUNT=$(echo "$PAGES" | jq 'length')
echo "Total pages: $COUNT"

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
const { execSync } = require('child_process');

// Get all entries
const output = execSync('marvin publish entries --json', { encoding: 'utf-8' });
const entries = JSON.parse(output);

// Filter by entry type
const pages = entries.filter(e => e.entryType === 'page');
const projects = entries.filter(e => e.entryType === 'project');

console.log(`Pages: ${pages.length}`);
console.log(`Projects: ${projects.length}`);

// Get single entry
const aboutOutput = execSync('marvin publish entry about --json', { encoding: 'utf-8' });
const [about] = JSON.parse(aboutOutput);

console.log(`Title: ${about.title}`);
console.log(`Published: ${about.publishedAt}`);

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
import subprocess
import json

# Get all entries
result = subprocess.run(
    ['marvin', 'publish', 'entries', '--json'],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True
)

entries = json.loads(result.stdout)

# Group by entry type
by_type = {}
for entry in entries:
    entry_type = entry['entryType']
    if entry_type not in by_type:
        by_type[entry_type] = []
    by_type[entry_type].append(entry)

# Print summary
for entry_type, items in by_type.items():
    print(f"{entry_type}: {len(items)}")

# Get single entry
result = subprocess.run(
    ['marvin', 'publish', 'entry', 'about', '--json'],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True
)

about = json.loads(result.stdout)[0]
print(f"About page title: {about['title']}")

docs.title: Static Site Generation (Astro)
docs.text:
// scripts/fetch-entries.js
const { execSync } = require('child_process');
const fs = require('fs');

// Fetch all entries
const entries = JSON.parse(
  execSync('marvin publish entries --json', { encoding: 'utf-8' })
);

// Save to data directory
fs.writeFileSync(
  'src/data/entries.json',
  JSON.stringify(entries, null, 2)
);

console.log(`Fetched ${entries.length} entries`);

// Fetch individual entries for SSG
entries.forEach(entry => {
  const detail = execSync(
    `marvin publish entry ${entry.slug} --json`,
    { encoding: 'utf-8' }
  );

  fs.writeFileSync(
    `src/data/entries/${entry.slug}.json`,
    detail
  );
});

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Requires a site client token. Set in environment:

export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

Or pass via command line:

marvin publish entries --site-token marvin_sk_your_token

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
Site client token is invalid or missing:

export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

docs.title: Unknown slug (single entry)
docs.text:
An unknown slug is not an error: the command prints an empty result. Verify the slug:

# List all entries to verify slug
marvin publish entries --json | jq -r '.[].slug'

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
Entry is not published or site client doesn't have access:

# Check entry status in admin panel
# Ensure entry is published

docs.title: Empty Results
docs.text:
No entries match the filters:

# Check available entry types
marvin publish entries --json | jq -r '.[].entryType' | sort -u

# Check available collections
marvin publish collections --json | jq -r '.[].slug'

docs.title: Related Commands
docs.text:
• marvin publish collections - List collections
  • marvin publish collection-entries <slug> - List entries in a collection

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This command calls:

GET /api/publish/{workspace}/entries
GET /api/publish/{workspace}/entries/{slug}

Query parameters for the list endpoint include entry_type, collection, tag, slug, updated_since, expand, limit and offset.

See API Mapping for more details.

docs.title: Entry Types
docs.text: Entry types define the kinds of content in a workspace (pages, posts, products, ...): their schema, how they render, what they can do, and their authoring recipe. List and inspect them, or create, change and delete your own.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform entry-types list
marvin platform entry-types get <id>
marvin platform entry-types create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform entry-types update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform entry-types delete <id> --yes

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path. With neither, create and update read piped stdin.

Required role

Listing and reading entry types is open to any workspace member. Creating, updating or deleting one needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
List the workspace's entry types.

marvin platform entry-types list
marvin platform entry-types list --json | jq -r '.[].slug'

Columns: ID, Name, Slug, System, Renderer, Package, Publishable (yes/no), Routable (yes/no). Renderer and Package come from the type's renderingJson, Publishable and Routable from its capabilitiesJson; a type with no capabilities shows them blank.

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Print one entry type with its full definition.

marvin platform entry-types get 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef --json | jq '.schemaJson'
Argument Description <id> Entry type ID

The record carries name, slug, description, icon, color, sortOrder, isSystem, isRendered, and the JSON blocks schemaJson (field definitions), renderingJson, capabilitiesJson and recipeJson.

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Create an entry type from a JSON body. name is required; slug, description, icon, color, sortOrder, isRendered, schemaJson, renderingJson, capabilitiesJson and recipeJson are optional.

marvin platform entry-types create --data '{"name": "Lookbook", "slug": "lookbook"}'
marvin platform entry-types create --file lookbook.json
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Entry type data as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the entry type data (same as --data @path)

Prints ✓ Created entry type: <id> on stderr and the new entry type on stdout.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Change an entry type. The body holds only the fields to change.

marvin platform entry-types update 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef --data '{"description": "Seasonal lookbooks"}'
Argument Description <id> Entry type ID Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Entry type data as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the entry type data (same as --data @path)

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Delete an entry type.

marvin platform entry-types delete 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef --yes
Argument Description <id> Entry type ID Option Description Default --yes Confirm the deletion; the command refuses to run without it

In --json mode the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
# Slug and name of every entry type
marvin platform entry-types list --json | jq -r '.[] | "\(.slug)\t\(.name)"'

# Entry types that can't be published
marvin platform entry-types list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.capabilitiesJson.publishable == false) | .slug'

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Renderers - the renderer packages an entry type's renderingJson points at
  • Platform entries - creating entries of a given type

docs.title: Event Log
docs.text:
The workspace's audit trail: a record of what happened to which entity, and who did it. Filter the log, follow one entity or one user, and list the event types that subscriptions and workflows can react to. The commands are marvin platform event-log ….

platform events is deprecated

marvin platform events … is an old alias of platform event-log. It still works in 3.x with a warning on stderr and is removed in 4.0. marvin events is a different command: the Events hub, what sends each event type and what reacts to it.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform event-log list [--event-type <type>] [--entity-type <type>] [--entity-id <id>] [--user-id <id>] [--start-date <date>] [--end-date <date>] [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>]
marvin platform event-log get <event-id>
marvin platform event-log entity <entity-id> [--entity-type <type>] [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>]
marvin platform event-log user <user-id> [--event-type <type>] [--start-date <date>] [--end-date <date>] [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>]
marvin platform event-log types

Any workspace member can run these commands. Dates are ISO 8601 (2026-07-01 or 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z).

docs.title: list
docs.text:
List events, newest first, optionally filtered.

marvin platform event-log list --event-type entry.published --limit 20
marvin platform event-log list --user-id 8a1f… --start-date 2026-07-01 --end-date 2026-07-31
Option Description Default --event-type <type> Filter by event type (e.g. entry.published) --entity-type <type> Filter by entity type (e.g. entry, asset) --entity-id <id> Filter by entity ID --user-id <id> Filter by user ID --start-date <date> Only events on or after this date --end-date <date> Only events on or before this date --limit <number> Maximum number of events to return 50 --offset <number> Number of events to skip 0

Columns: ID (the event id), Event, Occurred, User, Entity Type, Title.

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Print one event in full, including its eventData payload.

marvin platform event-log get 5d0c2b7e-3f1a-4c8e-9b64-0a7e12f4d3c1 --json | jq '.eventData'
Argument Description <event-id> Event ID (the ID column of list)

docs.title: entity
docs.text:
Show the complete event history of one entity, such as an entry or an asset.

marvin platform event-log entity 6f1c9a40-… --entity-type entry
Argument Description <entity-id> ID of the entry, asset or other entity Option Description Default --entity-type <type> Filter by entity type (e.g. entry, asset) --limit <number> Maximum number of events to return 100 --offset <number> Number of events to skip 0

Columns: ID, Event, Occurred, User, Title.

docs.title: user
docs.text:
Show what one user did.

marvin platform event-log user 8a1f… --start-date 2026-07-01 --event-type entry.published
Argument Description <user-id> User ID Option Description Default --event-type <type> Filter by event type (e.g. entry.published) --start-date <date> Only events on or after this date --end-date <date> Only events on or before this date --limit <number> Maximum number of events to return 100 --offset <number> Number of events to skip 0

Columns: ID, Event, Occurred, Entity Type, Entity ID, Title.

docs.title: types
docs.text:
List the subscribable event types and the variables each one carries. These are the events that email subscriptions, integration subscriptions and workflow triggers react to.

marvin platform event-log types
marvin platform event-log types --json | jq -r '.[].value'

Columns: value, label, category, description. --json also includes each type's variables.

docs.title: Paging
docs.text:
--limit and --offset page through a long log:

marvin platform event-log list --limit 50 --offset 0     # page 1
marvin platform event-log list --limit 50 --offset 50    # page 2

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
# Events per type since the start of the month
marvin platform event-log list --start-date 2026-07-01 --limit 1000 --json \
  | jq -r '.[].eventType' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Who published what, as CSV
marvin platform event-log list --event-type entry.published --csv

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Events hub - what sends each event type and what reacts to it
  • Workflows - triggers that react to these events
  • Integrations - integration subscriptions to event types

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The Events hub answers two questions about every event type in a workspace: what sends it, and what happens when it does. It is the CLI side of the admin app's Events page.

marvin events is about event types. To read the individual events that happened, use marvin platform event-log. Its old alias platform events is deprecated and removed in 4.0.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin events list [--category <name>] [--connected | --unused]
marvin events show <event-type> [--limit <n>]

Required role

Both commands need the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role: they show the workspace's workflows, integrations, webhooks and email subscriptions. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
marvin events list
marvin events list --connected          # types something reacts to
marvin events list --unused             # types nothing reacts to
marvin events list --category content   # one category (case doesn't matter)
marvin events list --category —         # types with no category
Option Description Default --category <name> Only event types in this category (e.g. Content) --connected Only event types something reacts to (built-ins don't count) --unused Only event types nothing reacts to (built-ins don't count)

--connected and --unused can't be combined. One row per workspace event type, in catalogue order:

Column Meaning Event type The type's key, e.g. entry_published Name, Category The type's own, or else the event catalogue's; a type neither names shows its key as the name and — as the category Senders How many things send it: Marvin itself, workflows, incoming webhooks, scheduled tasks Reactions (on/total) Workflows, integration actions, emails and webhooks that react to it: switched on / all Built-in Reactions Marvin always runs, such as queueing a site rebuild Last occurred When it last happened, or blank

--connected and --unused look at reactions you can configure, so built-ins don't count: a type with only built-in reactions is --unused. Platform-scope event types are not listed; the admin Events page shows those.

With --json each row is the API's summary row with name and category filled in as above (category is null rather than — when there is none):

{
  "eventType": "entry_published",
  "name": "Entry Published",
  "category": "Content",
  "senders": 5,
  "reactions": 1,
  "activeReactions": 1,
  "builtinReactions": 4,
  "lastOccurredAt": "2026-10-04T18:02:23.857734Z"
}

# Event types nobody has wired up yet
marvin events list --unused --json | jq -r '.[].eventType'

docs.title: Show
docs.text:
marvin events show entry_published
marvin events show entry_published --limit 25
Argument / option Description Default <event-type> The event type's key, e.g. entry_published --limit <n> How many recent events to show (at most 50) 10

In a terminal it prints a page:

Entry Published (entry_published)
Category: Content
A content entry was published.
Recorded in the event log: yes

Sent by
  on   Marvin            Publishing an entry (app, API, CLI)
  on   Workflow          Buttondown: subscriber confirmed — Entry step: publish · installed by Buttondown
  on   Incoming webhook  Buttondown events — Starts the workflow Buttondown: subscriber confirmed · installed by Buttondown
  on   Scheduled task    Publish Scheduled Entries — System task (every workspace)

What happens
  Workflows
    on   Buttondown: email an issue when published — installed by Buttondown
  Built-in
    on   Refreshes AI search
    on   Queues a site rebuild

Recent (newest first, UTC)
  2026-10-04 18:02  Entry 'Studio Notes' published

Leads to: site_rebuild_queued (Site Rebuild Queued), ai_embeddings_reindexed (AI Embeddings Reindexed)
Caused by: nothing
  • Sent by: each sender with its kind and whether it is switched on.
  • What happens: reactions grouped by kind (workflows, integration actions, webhooks, emails), built-ins last. "installed by" names the integration whose blueprint created it.
  • Recent: the newest --limit events (default 10, at most 50). A type that isn't recorded in the event log has no history.
  • Leads to / Caused by: event types this one sets off, and the ones that set it off.

With --json (or --yaml) it prints the API object unchanged: eventType, name, description, category, audited, senders[], reactions[], recent[], leadsTo[], causedBy[].

# Reactions that are switched off
marvin events show entry_published --json | jq '.reactions[] | select(.enabled | not) | .name'

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
An event type the workspace doesn't have, or a platform event type, is a 404:

✗ API Error (404)
Unknown event type 'nope' (or a platform event — see the admin Events page)

With --json: {"error": "Unknown event type 'nope' (or a platform event — see the admin Events page)", "status": 404}. Without the ADMIN role, both commands answer with the usual permission message.

docs.title: Forms
docs.text: Forms collect submissions from your site. These commands manage form definitions, read the submissions they have received, and call the public Publishing API endpoints for a published form.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform forms list
marvin platform forms get <id>
marvin platform forms create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform forms update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform forms delete <id> --yes
marvin platform forms submissions <formId> [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>]
marvin platform forms get-published <slug>
marvin platform forms submit <slug> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)

Required role

Any member lists and reads forms. Creating, updating and deleting a form needs ADMIN (or OWNER); reading a form's submissions needs EDITOR. See Workspace roles.

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path. With neither, the command reads piped stdin.

docs.title: The form object
docs.text:
Field Description Default name Form name (required on create) slug URL identifier; generated by the server when omitted description Free text none status Form status draft formSchema Object describing the form's fields {} settingsJson Form settings object none metadataJson Free-form metadata object none

update takes any subset of these fields.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform forms list
marvin platform forms get 4d0c8e2a-91b3-4f6a-b7c5-3e1a2f9d6b80 --json

list columns: ID, Slug, Name, Status, Submissions (count), Created. <id> is the form's UUID.

docs.title: Create, update, delete
docs.text:
marvin platform forms create --data '{
  "name": "Contact",
  "slug": "contact",
  "description": "Website contact form",
  "formSchema": {"fields": []}
}'

marvin platform forms update 4d0c8e2a-91b3-4f6a-b7c5-3e1a2f9d6b80 --data '{"description": "Contact us"}'
marvin platform forms delete 4d0c8e2a-91b3-4f6a-b7c5-3e1a2f9d6b80 --yes

create and update print Created form: <id> (<slug>) / Updated form: ... on stderr and the form on stdout. delete requires --yes (without it the command exits 1); with --json it prints {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Submissions
docs.text:
marvin platform forms submissions 4d0c8e2a-91b3-4f6a-b7c5-3e1a2f9d6b80
marvin platform forms submissions 4d0c8e2a-91b3-4f6a-b7c5-3e1a2f9d6b80 --limit 20 --offset 20 --json

Lists a form's submissions, newest first.

Option Description Default --limit <number> Maximum number of submissions to return (a positive integer) 100 --offset <number> Number of submissions to skip (0 or more) 0

Columns: ID, Status, Submitted At, IP. --json also has dataJson (what the visitor sent), metadataJson, userAgent, referrer and processedAt:

marvin platform forms submissions 4d0c8e2a-91b3-4f6a-b7c5-3e1a2f9d6b80 --json | jq '.[].dataJson'

docs.title: Published forms (Publishing API)
docs.text:
marvin platform forms get-published contact
marvin platform forms submit contact --data '{"name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com", "message": "Hello"}'

Both resolve the current workspace's slug and call the public endpoint for the form with the given <slug> (the form's slug, not its id).

  • get-published prints the published form definition.
  • submit sends the JSON body as a submission, prints Submitted to form: <slug> on stderr and the stored submission on stdout.

docs.title: Incoming Webhooks
docs.text: An incoming webhook is a URL an outside service POSTs to. Each delivery drops an incoming_webhook event carrying the request body, which a workflow with an incoming_webhook trigger reacts to. The URL is <api-url>/api/hooks/<token>: the token is the credential, and you can rotate or revoke it. A webhook can also verify each delivery's signature.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform incoming-webhooks list
marvin platform incoming-webhooks get <webhook>
marvin platform incoming-webhooks create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform incoming-webhooks update <webhook> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform incoming-webhooks delete <webhook> --yes
marvin platform incoming-webhooks mint-token <webhook>
marvin platform incoming-webhooks revoke-token <webhook>
marvin platform incoming-webhooks signature-schemes

Every command that takes <webhook> accepts its id or its slug. --data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path.

Required role

Every incoming-webhook command, reads included, needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role: the token is a credential. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: create and mint-token
docs.text:
A new webhook has no token, so nothing can call it yet. Mint one to get the URL:

marvin platform incoming-webhooks create --data '{"name": "Shopify orders", "enabled": true}'
marvin platform incoming-webhooks mint-token shopify-orders
# ✓ Minted a token for shopify-orders. Senders POST to: https://cms.example.com/api/hooks/…

The URL goes to stderr; stdout carries the webhook (with its token), so mint-token … --json | jq -r .token works in a script. Minting again rotates the token: the old URL stops working at once. revoke-token leaves the webhook without a token until you mint a new one.

Command Argument / option Description create --data <json\|@file\|-> The webhook as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the webhook (same as --data @path) update <webhook> Webhook id or slug --data <json\|@file\|->, --file <path> The fields to change, as for create mint-token <webhook> Webhook id or slug; no options revoke-token <webhook> Webhook id or slug; no options

The body for create/update:

Field Meaning name Display name (required on create) slug Defaults to one made from the name; fixed after create description Free text enabled false (the default) rejects deliveries signingSecretRef Slug of the workspace secret that holds the sender's signing key signatureScheme How to check the signature: a scheme from signature-schemes signatureHeader The header carrying the signature, when the scheme lets you choose signatureUrl The URL the sender signs, for schemes that sign it (when it differs from the receiver's) signatureConfig The construction, for custom

revoke-token makes the receiver reject every request until a new token is minted:

marvin platform incoming-webhooks revoke-token shopify-orders

docs.title: update and signature-schemes
docs.text:
marvin platform incoming-webhooks update shopify-orders --data '{"enabled": true}'
marvin platform incoming-webhooks signature-schemes

signature-schemes takes no options. It lists the schemes: core presets (GitHub-style HMAC, Slack, Stripe, Standard Webhooks, a static token, …), presets that installed integrations contribute, and custom. Source says where each comes from. Store the sender's key as a workspace secret, then point the webhook at it:

marvin platform secrets create --name "Stripe signing key" --value-stdin < key.txt
marvin platform incoming-webhooks update stripe-events \
  --data '{"signatureScheme": "stripe", "signingSecretRef": "stripe-signing-key"}'

The server refuses a scheme it can't verify with (unknown, or a custom config that doesn't describe a usable construction) with a 422 that says why.

docs.title: list and get
docs.text:
marvin platform incoming-webhooks list
marvin platform incoming-webhooks get shopify-orders --json | jq -r .token

get takes <webhook> and no options; it prints the webhook including its token.

Columns: ID, Slug, Name, Enabled, Token (minted or none; the value is only shown by get), Signature (the scheme, hmac-sha256 for the default check, or none), Received, Last received.

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
marvin platform incoming-webhooks delete shopify-orders --yes
Argument / option Description Default <webhook> Webhook id or slug --yes Confirm the delete; the command refuses to run without it

The URL stops working. Prints {"deleted": "<id>"} with --json.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Manage the workspace's integrations: connections to providers such as Slack, Apprise, n8n or Cloudflare Pages, the event subscriptions that run their actions, and how their errors are handled.

Required role

Every integration command needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role, except providers, which any member can run. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

Server requirement

The integration routes only exist when the Marvin server has the integration SDK (marvin-integration-sdk) installed. Without it every command here answers 404.

Every command that takes <integration> accepts the integration's id or its slug (the CLI looks it up in the list; the API has no single-integration route).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations list [--needs-attention]
marvin platform integrations get <integration>
marvin platform integrations providers
marvin platform integrations plugins
marvin platform integrations create --data <json|@file|-> [--credential-stdin]
marvin platform integrations update <integration> [--data <json|@file|->] [--credential-stdin]
marvin platform integrations delete <integration> --yes
marvin platform integrations check <integration>
marvin platform integrations resolve <integration> [--alert-id <id>]
marvin platform integrations run <integration> <action> [--data <json|@file|->]
marvin platform integrations options <integration> <action> <input>

marvin platform integrations errors <integration>
marvin platform integrations errors set <integration> <code> [--review|--no-review] [--alert|--no-alert]
marvin platform integrations errors reset <integration> [code]

marvin platform integrations alert-routing
marvin platform integrations alert-routing set [--email-admins|--no-email-admins] [--targets <ids>] [--reminder-hours <n>]

marvin platform integrations subscriptions list [--event <type>]
marvin platform integrations subscriptions create (--data <json|@file|-> | --integration <id> --event <type> --action <key> [--args <json>])
marvin platform integrations subscriptions update <id> [--enable|--disable] [--args <json>] [--data <json|@file|->]
marvin platform integrations subscriptions delete <id> --yes

subscriptions also answers to subs (the examples below use both). --data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations list
marvin platform integrations list --needs-attention --json

Columns: ID, Slug, Name, Provider, Enabled, Status (ok, error, unconfigured), and Attention: the integration's open alerts, e.g. ⚠ 3 (rate_limited) — how many failures and which error codes. When any integration needs attention, table mode adds a line on stderr pointing at get and resolve.

Option Description Default --needs-attention Only integrations with open alerts 
marvin platform integrations get team-slack --json

<integration> is the integration's id or slug. Prints the integration: config, whether it has a credential, status, last check, open alerts (attention, with sample failures) and errorOverrides.

docs.title: Providers and plugins
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations providers
marvin platform integrations plugins

providers lists what can be connected. Columns: Slug, Name, Category, Actions (their keys), Emits (how many events it emits), Logo. In JSON mode each provider also has a logoUrl — the public logo route, built by the client — when the provider ships a logo (hasLogo), otherwise null (use icon).

plugins lists the plugin packages that supply providers, whether each loaded (and why not), the provider slugs it adds, and its version (columns: Name, Source, Loaded, Providers, Version). Both take no options. Platform admins can see every installed plugin, integration and AI, with marvin admin system plugins.

docs.title: Create, update, delete
docs.text:
pass show slack/bot-token | marvin platform integrations create \
  --data '{"provider":"slack","name":"Team Slack","config":{}}' --credential-stdin

marvin platform integrations update team-slack --data '{"enabled":false}'
pass show slack/bot-token-2 | marvin platform integrations update team-slack --credential-stdin
marvin platform integrations delete team-slack --yes
Argument / option Applies to Description Default <integration> update, delete Integration id or slug --data <json\|@file\|-> create, update The integration (create) or the fields to change (update) as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> create, update JSON file with the same (same as --data @path) --credential-stdin create, update Read the provider credential (API key, token) from stdin --yes delete Confirm the delete; the command refuses to run without it

create needs a body; update needs --data/--file and/or --credential-stdin. The create body is {provider, name, slug?, config?, credential?}; update takes any of name, enabled, config, credential. Pass the credential (API key, token) with --credential-stdin rather than in --data, so it stays out of your shell history; it is merged into the body as credential. --credential-stdin can't be combined with --data - (both read stdin).

delete removes the integration and its event subscriptions, and prints {"deleted": "<id>"} in JSON mode.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations check team-slack

Takes <integration> (id or slug); no options. Tests the connection now and prints {"ok": <status is ok>, "status": ..., "lastError": ...} in JSON mode. Exits 1 unless the status comes back ok.

docs.title: resolve
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations resolve team-slack
marvin platform integrations resolve team-slack --alert-id <alert-id>
Argument / option Description Default <integration> Integration id or slug --alert-id <id> Resolve just this alert all open alerts

Marks the integration's open alerts resolved ("I fixed it"), or one alert with --alert-id. The resolution is announced through the channels that delivered each alert, and retries parked behind the alert run again. Prints {"ok": true, "resolved": <count>} in JSON mode.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations run team-slack post_message --data '{"channel":"C123","text":"Hello"}'
Argument / option Description Default <integration> Integration id or slug <action> The provider's action key (see providers) --data <json\|@file\|-> The action's arguments as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin {} --file <path> JSON file with the arguments (same as --data @path)

Runs one of the provider's actions now with the given arguments ({{SLUG}} placeholders are resolved from workspace secrets). The integration must be enabled. Prints {"ok": ..., "result": {...}} and exits 1 when the action reports failure.

docs.title: options
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations options team-slack post_message channel

Takes <integration>, <action> and <input> (the action input's name); no options. Lists the choices for an action input that offers them (here, the Slack channels), as Value and Label columns.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Each provider declares an error policy: for every error code it can raise (for the provider as a whole, and per action), what happens when a workflow step fails with it — retry with backoff, send the entry to review, alert the workspace admins, or treat it as a success.

marvin platform integrations errors team-slack

Takes <integration> (id or slug); no options. Prints the policy table for this connection:

Column Meaning Scope provider, or action <key> for an action's own codes Code The error code Provider default What the provider does, e.g. retry 3× (1m, 5m, 30m), then send to review Review Whether the entry goes to review, after this connection's overrides Alert Whether workspace admins are alerted, after this connection's overrides Override What this connection changed, if anything

A connection can override two things per code: review and alert (the API calls it notify). Retries always stay the provider's. An override for a specific code wins; otherwise an override for * applies to every code; otherwise the provider's default.

# Don't send rate-limited posts to review, but do alert
marvin platform integrations errors set team-slack rate_limited --no-review --alert

# Silence alerts for every code on this connection
marvin platform integrations errors set team-slack '*' --no-alert

# Drop one override, or all of them
marvin platform integrations errors reset team-slack rate_limited
marvin platform integrations errors reset team-slack
Command Argument / option Description errors set <integration> Integration id or slug <code> The error code, or * for every code --review / --no-review Send the entry to review when this error happens / don't --alert / --no-alert Alert the workspace admins / don't errors reset <integration> Integration id or slug [code] The code whose override to drop; omit to drop every override

errors set merges into the connection's existing overrides and needs at least one of --review/--no-review, --alert/--no-alert. The server rejects a code the provider doesn't declare. Both set and reset print the connection's overrides afterwards. reset <integration> <code> fails if there is no override for that code.

docs.title: Alert routing
docs.text:
marvin platform integrations alert-routing
marvin platform integrations alert-routing set --no-email-admins --targets <id>,<id> --reminder-hours 12

Where integration alerts go: email to the workspace admins, and/or notify-capable integrations (targets). Bare alert-routing shows the current routing (in table mode: whether admins are emailed, the reminder interval, and a table of the target integrations); it takes no options.

alert-routing set needs at least one option:

Option Description Default --email-admins / --no-email-admins Email the workspace admins / don't --targets <ids> Comma-separated integration ids to alert through; replaces the list ('' for none) --reminder-hours <n> Re-alert an unresolved problem every n hours

docs.title: Event subscriptions
docs.text:
An event subscription runs an integration action whenever an event happens — for example, post to Slack when an entry is published. marvin platform event-log types lists the event types and the variables each one carries for --args templates.

marvin platform integrations subscriptions list
marvin platform integrations subscriptions list --event entry_published

marvin platform integrations subscriptions create --integration team-slack \
  --event entry_published --action post_message --args '{"text":"New: {{entry.title}}"}'

marvin platform integrations subs update <id> --disable
marvin platform integrations subs update <id> --args '{"text":"Published: {{entry.title}}"}'
marvin platform integrations subs delete <id> --yes

Subscription list columns: ID, Event, Integration, Action, Enabled.

Command Option Description Default list --event <type> Only subscriptions to this event type create --integration <id> Integration id or slug --event <type> Event type (see platform event-log types) --action <key> Provider action to run --args <json> Action arguments as JSON (templated: {{entry.title}}, {{SECRET}}) --data <json\|@file\|-> {integrationId, eventType, action, args?} as JSON, @path or -; instead of the three flags --file <path> JSON file with the same (same as --data @path) update <id> --enable / --disable Turn it on / off (not both) --args <json> Replace the action arguments --data <json\|@file\|->, --file <path> {enabled?, args?} as JSON, @path or - delete <id> --yes Confirm the delete; the command refuses to run without it

create takes either the three flags (--integration accepts an id or slug) or a {integrationId, eventType, action, args?} body with --data. update takes --enable, --disable, --args and/or --data '{enabled?, args?}'.

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
stdout carries data only; ✓ lines and the attention hint go to stderr.

# Fail a health check if any integration needs attention
n=$(marvin platform integrations list --needs-attention --json | jq length)
[ "$n" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

# Re-check every enabled integration
marvin platform integrations list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.enabled) | .slug' |
  while read -r slug; do marvin platform integrations check "$slug" || echo "$slug failed" >&2; done

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Command Endpoint list, get GET /api/groups/integrations providers GET /api/groups/integrations/providers plugins GET /api/groups/integrations/plugins create POST /api/groups/integrations update PATCH /api/groups/integrations/{id} delete DELETE /api/groups/integrations/{id} check POST /api/groups/integrations/{id}/check resolve POST /api/groups/integrations/{id}/resolve run POST /api/groups/integrations/{id}/actions/{action_key} options POST /api/groups/integrations/{id}/options errors GET /api/groups/integrations + GET /api/groups/integrations/providers errors set, errors reset PUT /api/groups/integrations/{id}/error-overrides alert-routing GET / PUT /api/groups/integrations/alert-routing subscriptions GET / POST /api/groups/integrations/subscriptions, PATCH / DELETE …/subscriptions/{id}

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Workflows — integration actions, and the run history that shows how failures were handled
  • Site rebuild — an integration (e.g. Cloudflare Pages) can be what builds the site

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text: The Marvin CLI supports four output formats to suit different use cases: table, JSON, YAML, and CSV.

docs.title: Available Formats
docs.text: Format Use Case Flag Table Human-readable terminal output Default JSON Machine-readable, scripting, APIs --json or --output json YAML Human-readable, configuration files --yaml or --output yaml CSV Spreadsheets, data analysis --csv or --output csv

docs.title: stdout vs stderr
docs.text:
stdout carries data only. Everything meant for a person goes to stderr: ✓ Created… confirmations, progress lines, hints and warnings (including deprecation warnings). So --json | jq always gets one clean JSON document, and 2>/dev/null hides the chatter without losing data.

What each kind of command prints on stdout in JSON, YAML or CSV mode:

Command kind stdout list / get the items or the object create / update the created or updated resource delete / remove / revoke {"deleted": "<id>"} run / test / rerun / import and other actions {"ok": true, ...} plus whatever the server returned any error {"error": "...", "status": 403, ...}, and the exit code is 1

In table mode a delete or an action prints only its ✓ line, on stderr, so stdout is empty.

id=$(marvin platform entries create --data @entry.json --json | jq -r .id)
marvin platform entries delete "$id" --yes --json        # {"deleted": "<id>"}
marvin platform webhooks test "$id" --json | jq .ok      # true

Write commands take their body with --data: inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin (--file <path> is the same as --data @path). The old --json '<payload>' spelling still works in 3.x with a warning on stderr and is removed in 4.0.

docs.title: Table Format
docs.text: Default format for human-readable output in the terminal.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
marvin publish entries
# Or explicitly
marvin publish entries --output table

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Automatic column sizing
  • Unicode box-drawing characters
  • Truncates long values to fit terminal width
  • Color highlighting (when supported)

docs.title: Best For
docs.text:
• Quick inspection in terminal
  • Development and debugging
  • Manual verification

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text: Machine-readable format for scripting and automation.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
marvin publish entries --json
# Or
marvin publish entries --output json

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
[
  {
    "slug": "home",
    "title": "Homepage",
    "entryType": "page",
    "status": "published",
    "publishedAt": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  {
    "slug": "about",
    "title": "About Us",
    "entryType": "page",
    "status": "published",
    "publishedAt": "2026-07-02T00:00:00Z"
  }
]

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Valid JSON output
  • Preserves data types (numbers, booleans, null)
  • Nested objects and arrays
  • ISO 8601 dates

docs.title: Best For
docs.text:
• Piping to jq for processing
  • Saving to files for later use
  • Parsing in scripts (Node.js, Python, etc.)
  • API integrations

docs.title: Processing with jq
docs.text:
# Extract titles
marvin publish entries --json | jq -r '.[].title'

# Filter by entry type
marvin publish entries --json | jq '.[] | select(.entryType == "page")'

# Count entries
marvin publish entries --json | jq 'length'

# Get specific fields
marvin publish entries --json | jq '.[] | {title, slug}'

docs.title: YAML Format
docs.text: Human-readable format, easier to read than JSON for complex data.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
marvin publish entries --yaml
# Or
marvin publish entries --output yaml

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
- slug: home
  title: Homepage
  entryType: page
  status: published
  publishedAt: 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z
- slug: about
  title: About Us
  entryType: page
  status: published
  publishedAt: 2026-07-02T00:00:00Z

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Readable indentation
  • No quotes needed for most strings
  • Comments supported (when editing)
  • Multiline strings

docs.title: Best For
docs.text:
• Configuration files
  • Documentation
  • Human review of structured data
  • Version control diffs

docs.title: Processing with yq
docs.text:
# Extract titles
marvin publish entries --yaml | yq '.[] | .title'

# Filter entries
marvin publish entries --yaml | yq '.[] | select(.entryType == "page")'

# Convert to JSON
marvin publish entries --yaml | yq -o json

docs.title: CSV Format
docs.text: Spreadsheet-compatible format for data analysis.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
marvin publish entries --csv
# Or
marvin publish entries --output csv

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
Title,Slug,Type,Status,Published
Homepage,home,page,published,2026-07-01
About Us,about,page,published,2026-07-02
Contact,contact,page,published,2026-07-03

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Standard CSV format (RFC 4180)
  • Header row with column names
  • Quoted fields when needed
  • Escaped commas and quotes

docs.title: Best For
docs.text:
• Excel/Google Sheets import
  • Data analysis with pandas/R
  • Bulk operations
  • Reporting

docs.title: Importing to Spreadsheets
docs.text:
# Export to file
marvin publish entries --csv > entries.csv

# Open in Excel (macOS)
open entries.csv

# Import to Google Sheets
# Upload the CSV file

docs.title: Processing with Tools
docs.text:
# Count rows (excluding header)
marvin publish entries --csv | tail -n +2 | wc -l

# Extract specific column
marvin publish entries --csv | cut -d',' -f1

# Sort by column
marvin publish entries --csv | sort -t',' -k3

docs.title: Command-Line Flags
docs.text:
# Long form
marvin publish entries --output json
marvin publish entries --output yaml
marvin publish entries --output csv
marvin publish entries --output table

# Short form
marvin publish entries --json
marvin publish entries --yaml
marvin publish entries --csv

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text: If more than one is given, --json wins, then --yaml, then --csv, then --output <format>; with none of them the default comes from the MARVIN_OUTPUT_FORMAT environment variable (table, json, yaml or csv), and without that the format is table. A flag always beats the variable. An unsupported --output or MARVIN_OUTPUT_FORMAT value is an error.

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
# Quick check in terminal
marvin publish entries

# Detailed inspection
marvin publish entry homepage --json | jq .

docs.title: Data Export
docs.text:
# Export all entries to JSON
marvin publish entries --json > entries.json

# Export assets to CSV for tracking
marvin platform assets list --csv > assets-$(date +%Y%m%d).csv

# Export site config to YAML
marvin publish site --yaml > site-config.yaml

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
# Count published pages
PAGE_COUNT=$(marvin publish entries --entry-type page --json | jq 'length')
echo "Published pages: $PAGE_COUNT"

# Check if entry exists (an unknown slug prints [])
if [ "$(marvin publish entry homepage --json | jq 'length')" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Homepage is published"
fi

# Get all image assets
marvin platform assets list --json | jq '[.[] | select(.assetType == "image")]' | jq -r '.[].publicUrl'

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text:
# Generate weekly report
echo "Content Report - Week $(date +%W)"
echo "================================"
echo "Total Entries: $(marvin publish entries --json | jq 'length')"
echo "Total Collections: $(marvin publish collections --json | jq 'length')"
echo "Total Assets: $(marvin platform assets list --json | jq 'length')"

# Export to CSV for analysis
marvin publish entries --csv > report-$(date +%Y%m%d).csv

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
# Verify deployment in GitHub Actions
- name: Verify Content Published
  run: |
    COUNT=$(marvin publish entries --json | jq 'length')
    if [ $COUNT -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "✓ Content published: $COUNT entries"
    else
      echo "✗ No content published"
      exit 1
    fi

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
# Pretty-print with jq
marvin publish entries --json | jq .

# Compact output
marvin publish entries --json | jq -c .

# Sort keys
marvin publish entries --json | jq -S .

docs.title: YAML
docs.text:
# Validate YAML
marvin publish entries --yaml | yamllint -

# Convert to JSON
marvin publish entries --yaml | yq -o json > entries.json

docs.title: CSV
docs.text:
# Add timestamps
marvin publish entries --csv | awk -v date="$(date +%Y-%m-%d)" 'NR==1{print $0",ExportDate"} NR>1{print $0","date}'

# Filter rows
marvin publish entries --csv | grep "published"

docs.title: Table Format
docs.text:
• May truncate long values
  • Not suitable for machine parsing
  • Layout depends on terminal width

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
• More verbose than YAML
  • Harder to read for humans
  • No comments

docs.title: YAML Format
docs.text:
• Slower to parse than JSON
  • Whitespace-sensitive
  • Limited tool support vs JSON

docs.title: CSV Format
docs.text:
• Flattens nested data
  • Limited data types (all strings)
  • No standard for complex structures

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use table for terminal - Quick checks and manual inspection
  2. Use JSON for scripts - Reliable parsing, rich data types
  3. Use YAML for config - Human-readable structured data

  4. Use CSV for analysis - Import to spreadsheets and analysis tools

  5. Always validate - Check output format before piping to files

  6. Handle errors - Check exit codes in scripts
  7. Save to files - Redirect output rather than copying from terminal
  8. Version exports - Include dates in exported filenames

docs.title: Commands Overview
docs.text: The Marvin CLI is organised into a handful of command groups that map to different Marvin APIs, plus a few top-level commands for signing in.

docs.title: Command Structure
docs.text: marvin [global-options] <command-group> <command> [command-options]

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
Available on all commands:

Option Description Default --api-url <url> Override Marvin API URL MARVIN_API_URL --workspace <slug> Override workspace slug MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG --output <format> Output format: table, json, yaml, csv table --json Shortcut for --output json - --yaml Shortcut for --output yaml - --csv Shortcut for --output csv - --help Show help - --version Show version -

docs.title: Command Groups
docs.text:
Group Purpose Credential login, logout, register, forgot-password, reset-password Sign in, sign out, create an account, reset a password None (they save or clear credentials) workspace Switch workspace, site tokens, export, import, backups, preferences, stats User token publish Read-only Publishing API Site client token platform Workspace content and configuration (create, read, update, delete) User token admin Instance administration User token of a SUPER_ADMIN user Your own profile and personal API tokens User token events What sends each event type and what reacts to it User token system Health and version of the server None

publish is hidden from marvin --help until a site token is available, and workspace, platform, admin, user and events are hidden until a user token is available; hidden commands still run. See Authentication for how tokens are saved and resolved.

docs.title: Sign in (top level)
docs.text:
marvin login                      # prompts for a user token
marvin login --site-token <token> --workspace <slug>
marvin logout [--site-token | --all]
marvin register
marvin forgot-password <email>
marvin reset-password --token <token> --password <newPassword>

There is no marvin auth group and no whoami; use marvin user profile show.

Learn more: Authentication Commands

docs.title: Workspace (workspace)
docs.text:
marvin workspace current | use <workspace> | list
marvin workspace token | token:remove
marvin workspace export | import
marvin workspace preferences [update] | stats
marvin workspace backups list | create | download <filename>

Learn more: Workspaces

docs.title: Publishing API (publish)
docs.text:
Read-only commands for accessing published content. Uses a site client token (--site-token, a token saved with marvin workspace token, or MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN).

Command Description site Get workspace site configuration entries List published entries entry <slug> Get a single entry collections List collections collection <slug> Get a collection collection-entries <slug> List entries in a collection renderers List the renderers the workspace needs

Learn more: Site, Entries, Collections, Renderers. Assets and resources are carried inline on each entry (publish entry <slug>); the libraries are under Platform Assets and Platform Resources.

docs.title: Platform API (platform)
docs.text:
Full CRUD for workspace content and configuration. Uses a user token (MARVIN_USER_TOKEN or marvin login) and the active workspace.

Group Description Page entries Manage entries (all statuses) Platform Entries collections Manage collections (including smart collections) Platform Collections, Smart Collections resources Manage resources Platform Resources assets Manage assets Platform Assets entry-types Manage entry types Entry Types tags The shared tag vocabulary Tags forms Form definitions and submissions Forms webhooks Outgoing webhooks Webhooks incoming-webhooks URLs outside services POST to, to trigger workflows Incoming Webhooks workflows Triggers, conditions, actions and runs Workflows integrations Provider connections, event subscriptions, error handling Integrations scheduled-tasks Scheduled task automation Scheduled Tasks api-clients Publishing API tokens API Clients workspace-members, invites Members, roles and invitation tokens Workspace Members & Invites email-templates Workspace email templates Email Templates email, email-subscriptions Email settings, SMTP and event subscriptions Email secrets, variables Write-only secrets and plain-text variables Secrets & Variables event-log Event log and audit trail Event Log site Request a site rebuild and check its status Site Rebuild blueprints Ready-made collections, entry types, tasks and workflows Blueprints ai Providers, models, operations, executions and AI settings AI dashboard What needs attention: inbox, drafts, review, AI suggestions, failures Review Queue

Workspace-level commands (marvin workspace ...) are on the Workspaces page.

docs.title: Events (events)
docs.text: marvin events list and marvin events show <event-type> show what sends each event type and what reacts to it. See Events.

docs.title: Admin API (admin)
docs.text:
Instance administration. Requires a user token belonging to a SUPER_ADMIN.

Group Description Page users Manage users Users system System information and settings System maintenance, scheduled-tasks Maintenance information and system-wide scheduled tasks Maintenance & Scheduled Tasks backups System backups Backups email System email settings and templates Admin Email groups, workspace-members Workspaces and their memberships Groups & Members

docs.title: User (user)
docs.text: Self-service commands for the signed-in user: user profile, user tokens and user change-password. See User Account.

docs.title: System (system)
docs.text: marvin system health and marvin system version need no credentials. See Health & Version.

docs.title: Most Common Commands

marvin publish entries
marvin publish entry homepage

# Export data
marvin publish entries --json > entries.json
marvin publish collections --csv > collections.csv

# Filter results

marvin publish entries --collection featured

# Platform operations

marvin workspace list
marvin platform entries list
marvin platform entries create --data @entry.json

marvin workspace current                     # Active workspace
marvin platform workspace-members list <workspace-id>   # Members
marvin platform invites list                 # Invitations

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text: All commands support multiple output formats:

docs.title: JSON

Machine-readable JSON:

marvin publish entries --json

[
  {
    "slug": "home",
    "title": "Homepage",
    "entryType": "page",
    "status": "published",
    "publishedAt": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
]

Human-readable YAML:

- slug: home
  title: Homepage
  entryType: page
  status: published

docs.title: CSV
docs.text:
Spreadsheet-compatible CSV:

Title,Slug,Type,Status,Published
Homepage,home,page,published,2026-07-01

Learn more: Output Formats

docs.title: Command Help
docs.text:
Get help for any command:

# General help
marvin --help

# Command group help
marvin publish --help
marvin platform --help

# Specific command help

docs.title: Platform assets
docs.text: Upload, download, edit and delete the workspace's assets (images, documents and other files) through the Platform API. The Publishing API has no asset routes; published entries carry their assets, with public URLs, inline (marvin publish entry <slug> --json | jq .assets).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform assets list
marvin platform assets get <id>
marvin platform assets upload <path> --slug <slug> --name <name> [--alt-text <text>] [--description <text>] [--metadata <json>]
marvin platform assets download <id> [-o, --out-file <file>]
marvin platform assets update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform assets apply-suggestion <id>
marvin platform assets reject-suggestion <id>
marvin platform assets delete <id> --yes

Required role

Any member can list, get and download assets. Uploading needs AUTHOR. Update, delete, apply-suggestion and reject-suggestion need EDITOR. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Lists every asset. Columns: ID, Name, Slug, Type (MIME type), Dimensions, Alt (first 40 characters).

marvin platform assets list
marvin platform assets list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.mimeType | startswith("image/")) | .slug'

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Shows one asset in full: URL, type, size, checksum, dimensions, suggestionJson and so on.

marvin platform assets get 2b7e4c10-8a1d-4f3b-b6e2-5d9a0c7e1f42

docs.title: upload
docs.text:
Uploads a local file as a new asset. Reports the file name and size, then the new asset's id, public URL, type, MIME type, size, checksum and (for images) dimensions, followed by the asset itself in the chosen output format.

Option Description Default <path> Path of the file to upload required --slug <slug> Asset slug (URL-friendly identifier) required --name <name> Asset name required --alt-text <text> Alt text for accessibility none --description <text> Description of the asset none --metadata <json> Custom metadata as a JSON string none 
marvin platform assets upload ./hero.jpg --slug hero --name "Hero image" --alt-text "Model in a chore coat"
marvin platform assets upload ./brochure.pdf --slug brochure --name "Brochure" --metadata '{"year": 2026}' --json

docs.title: download
docs.text:
Downloads an asset's raw file. With -o the file is written to that path; without it the bytes go to stdout when stdout is piped or redirected. On a terminal, with no --out-file, the command refuses before downloading anything.

Option Description Default -o, --out-file <file> Write the file to this path instead of stdout stdout (piped only)

With --out-file and --json/--yaml, the result is {"ok": true, "file": "…", "bytes": …, "contentType": "…"}; in table mode a confirmation goes to stderr.

marvin platform assets download 2b7e… -o hero.jpg
marvin platform assets download 2b7e… > hero.jpg
marvin platform assets download 2b7e… | convert - -resize 400x hero-small.jpg

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Updates an asset's metadata with the fields in the JSON body (slug, name, alt_text, description, metadata, tag_ids). It does not replace the file. --data takes inline JSON, @path, or - for stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path.

marvin platform assets update 2b7e… --data '{"alt_text": "Model wearing a chore coat"}'
marvin platform assets update 2b7e… --file ./asset-changes.json

docs.title: apply-suggestion and reject-suggestion
docs.text:
When an AI operation (for example alt-text generation) writes back with approval required, its proposed changes are staged on the asset as suggestionJson. apply-suggestion commits them and clears the suggestion; reject-suggestion discards them. Both print the updated asset. See Review queue. To review AI-generated assets attached to an entry, use entries suggested-assets.

marvin platform assets apply-suggestion 2b7e…
marvin platform assets reject-suggestion 2b7e…

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Deletes an asset. Without --yes the command refuses and exits with an error.

Option Description Default --yes Confirm the delete off 
marvin platform assets delete 2b7e… --yes

docs.title: Platform Collections
docs.text: Collections group content (entries, assets or resources) under a name and a slug. A collection is either curated by hand or smart, in which case rules decide who is in it. This page covers every marvin platform collections command; the rules-driven parts are detailed in Smart Collections. For the read-only public view, see Publishing collections.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform collections list
marvin platform collections get <id>
marvin platform collections create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>) [--smart-rules <json|@file|->]
marvin platform collections update <id> [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>] [--smart-rules <json|@file|->]
marvin platform collections delete <id> --yes
marvin platform collections members <id>
marvin platform collections preview --rules <json|@file|-> [--target-type <type>] [--limit <n>]
marvin platform collections order [ids...] [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>]
marvin platform collections entries <id>
marvin platform collections reorder <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform collections update-entry <id> <entry-id> [--role <role>] [--metadata <json>] [--data <json|@file|->]

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path. With neither, create, update (without --smart-rules) and reorder read piped stdin.

Required role

Any member can run list, get, members and entries. create, update, delete, preview, order, reorder and update-entry need the workspace EDITOR role. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
List the workspace's collections.

marvin platform collections list

Columns: ID, Name, Slug, Description (first 50 characters).

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Print one collection in full.

marvin platform collections get 3c9e5a10-7d4b-4f0e-9a21-5b8c1d2e6f70 --json
Argument Description <id> Collection ID

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Create a collection from a JSON body: name is required; slug, description, icon, color, sortOrder, isPublic, targetType (entry, asset or resource), metadataJson and entryIds are optional.

marvin platform collections create --data '{"name": "Spring Lookbook", "slug": "spring-lookbook"}'
marvin platform collections create --data '{"name": "News"}' --smart-rules '{"tags": ["news"]}'
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Collection data as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the collection data (same as --data @path) --smart-rules <json\|@file\|-> Smart-collection rules; makes the collection smart (isSmart: true)

Prints ✓ Created collection: <id> on stderr and the new collection on stdout.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Change a collection's fields. The body holds only the fields to change.

marvin platform collections update spring-lookbook --data '{"description": "Spring 2027 picks"}'
marvin platform collections update 3c9e5a10-… --smart-rules @rules.json
Argument Description <id> Collection ID Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Collection data as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the collection data (same as --data @path) --smart-rules <json\|@file\|-> Replace the smart rules (and make the collection smart); needs no --data

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Delete a collection.

marvin platform collections delete 3c9e5a10-… --yes
Option Description Default --yes Confirm the deletion; the command refuses to run without it
