In --json mode the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
List a collection's members, whatever it groups: entries, assets or resources.

marvin platform collections members 3c9e5a10-…

Columns: ID, Type, Label, Slug. See Smart Collections.

docs.title: preview
docs.text:
Show what smart-collection rules would match, without saving anything. Needs --rules.

marvin platform collections preview --rules '{"tags": ["news"], "statuses": ["published"]}' --limit 5
Option Description Default --rules <json\|@file\|-> The rules, as a collection's smartRules (required) --target-type <type> What the rules select: entry, asset or resource entry --limit <number> How many matches to list (at most 50); the total counts them all 10

Details and output in Smart Collections.

docs.title: order
docs.text:
Set the order collections are listed in, system collections included. Give the ids in the order you want, or --data with explicit sortOrder values; not both.

marvin platform collections order 3c9e5a10-… 7a21b3c4-… 0f4d9e88-…
marvin platform collections order --data '[{"id": "3c9e5a10-…", "sortOrder": 10}, {"id": "7a21b3c4-…", "sortOrder": 20}]'
Argument Description [ids...] Collection IDs, in the order you want (sortOrder 0, 1, 2, …) Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> An array of {id, sortOrder} as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the array (same as --data @path)

Ids that don't belong to a collection in this workspace are skipped, and the command says how many. With --json it prints {"ok": true, "updated": <n>}.

docs.title: entries
docs.text:
List the entries in an (entry) collection, in the collection's order.

marvin platform collections entries spring-lookbook

Columns: Order, ID, Title, Status, Published. Unlike members, this lists entries only, with the fields of an entry row.

docs.title: reorder
docs.text:
Reorder the entries in a collection. The body is a non-empty array of {entryId, sortOrder}.

marvin platform collections reorder 3c9e5a10-… --data '[{"entryId": "6f1c…", "sortOrder": 0}, {"entryId": "a82d…", "sortOrder": 1}]'
Argument Description <id> Collection ID Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> An array of {entryId, sortOrder} as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with the array (same as --data @path)

With --json it prints {"ok": true, "reordered": <n>, "collectionId": "<id>"}. Don't reorder a smart collection by hand: its rules own the membership.

docs.title: update-entry
docs.text:
Set the junction fields of one entry within one collection: its role and metadataJson. Give --role, --metadata or --data.

marvin platform collections update-entry spring-lookbook 6f1c… --role hero
marvin platform collections update-entry spring-lookbook 6f1c… --metadata '{"caption": "Opening look"}'
Argument Description <id> Collection ID <entry-id> Entry ID Option Description Default --role <role> Role of the entry within the collection --metadata <json> Junction metadata as a JSON string (sent as metadataJson) --data <json\|@file\|-> Full junction payload; overrides --role and --metadata

With none of the three the command exits 1 with Provide --role, --metadata, or --data.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Smart Collections - rules, preview, members and order in detail
  • Platform entries - add-to-collection and remove-from-collection

docs.title: Platform entries
docs.text: Create, edit, schedule and organize the workspace's entries through the Platform API. For reading published content use the Publishing API entries instead.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform entries list [--status <status>[,<status>…]] [--entry-type <slug>] [--suggestions] [--limit <n>]
marvin platform entries counts
marvin platform entries get <id>
marvin platform entries create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform entries update <id> [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>] [--status <status>] [--publish-at <iso>] [--expire-at <iso>]
marvin platform entries delete <id> --yes
marvin platform entries suggested-assets list <entry-id>
marvin platform entries suggested-assets approve <entry-id> <asset-id>
marvin platform entries suggested-assets reject <entry-id> <asset-id>
marvin platform entries apply-suggestion <id>
marvin platform entries reject-suggestion <id>
marvin platform entries collections <id>
marvin platform entries add-to-collection <entry-id> <collection-id>
marvin platform entries remove-from-collection <entry-id> <collection-id>

Required role

Any member can list, count and get entries, list their collections and list suggested assets. Writes need AUTHOR for your own draft entries and EDITOR for anyone else's entry or to approve, publish or schedule one. See Workspace roles.

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin. --file <path> is the same as --data @path, and piped stdin works with neither flag. Create and update print the saved entry in the chosen output format.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Lists entries, newest first. The API has no filters, so the CLI fetches the list and filters it. Columns: ID, Title, Slug, Type, Status, Published.

Option Description Default --status <status> Only entries with this status (inbox, draft, needs_review, published, …); comma-separate several all --entry-type <slug> Only entries of this entry type (slug or id); an unknown type is an error all --suggestions Only entries with a pending AI suggestion off --limit <number> At most this many entries, applied after filtering all 
marvin platform entries list --status needs_review --entry-type post --limit 20
marvin platform entries list --suggestions --json | jq -r '.[].id'

docs.title: counts
docs.text:
How many entries are in each status, plus the total. Table and CSV output show Status and Count rows; JSON and YAML output is the API's object.

marvin platform entries counts
marvin platform entries counts --json

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Shows one entry in full, including suggestionJson when an AI suggestion is pending.

marvin platform entries get 6f1c2a9e-3b7d-4e0a-9c55-1d2f8a4b7e10 --json | jq .suggestionJson

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Creates an entry from a JSON body. The body is the Platform API's entry payload; the required fields are entryTypeId, title and status. Prints Created entry: <id> on stderr, then the entry.

marvin platform entries create --data '{
  "entryTypeId": "0b6c7d1e-5a42-4f8e-8d3a-92c1e5a7f301",
  "title": "Spring lookbook",
  "slug": "spring-lookbook",
  "status": "draft"
}'
marvin platform entries create --file ./new-entry.json

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Updates an entry. The three flags change status and schedule without a JSON body; with only flags the command does not read stdin. Flags win over the same field in --data (publish_at or publishAt).

Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Entry fields to change, as JSON, @path, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the fields (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none --status <status> Set the status (for example draft, needs_review, published, archived) unchanged --publish-at <iso> Schedule publishing at this ISO 8601 time; "" (or none) clears the schedule unchanged --expire-at <iso> Unpublish at this ISO 8601 time; "" (or none) clears it unchanged

Times that are not valid ISO 8601 are rejected before the API is called.

marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --status needs_review
marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --publish-at 2026-10-31T09:00:00Z
marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --publish-at ""
marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --data '{"title": "Spring lookbook 2026"}'

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Deletes an entry. Without --yes the command refuses and exits with an error.

Option Description Default --yes Confirm the delete off 
marvin platform entries delete 6f1c… --yes

docs.title: suggested-assets
docs.text:
AI media operations (for example background removal) can attach the asset they made to an entry as a suggestion. It stays out of published output until someone approves it. These commands are part of the review queue.

Command Purpose suggested-assets list <entry-id> The entry's assets that are still suggestions. Columns: ID, Slug, Name, Type, Operation, Derived from suggested-assets approve <entry-id> <asset-id> Keep it: it becomes a normal attached asset and reaches published output suggested-assets reject <entry-id> <asset-id> Drop it: unlink it, and delete the asset if nothing else uses it

Approve and reject print the updated entry.

marvin platform entries suggested-assets list 6f1c…
marvin platform entries suggested-assets approve 6f1c… 2b7e4c10-8a1d-4f3b-b6e2-5d9a0c7e1f42

docs.title: apply-suggestion and reject-suggestion
docs.text:
Commit or discard the entry's pending AI suggestion (the proposed changes staged in suggestionJson). Both print the updated entry. The same pair exists for assets and resources; the workflow is covered in Review queue.

marvin platform entries apply-suggestion 6f1c…
marvin platform entries reject-suggestion 6f1c…

docs.title: collections, add-to-collection, remove-from-collection
docs.text:
collections lists the collections an entry belongs to (columns: ID, Name, Slug, Description). add-to-collection and remove-from-collection change membership; in JSON modes they print {"ok": true, "entryId": "…", "collectionId": "…"} ("removed": true for removal). Manage the collections themselves with platform collections.

marvin platform entries collections 6f1c…
marvin platform entries add-to-collection 6f1c… 3d8e5f20-9b14-4c7a-a0e6-71c4b2d95a08
marvin platform entries remove-from-collection 6f1c… 3d8e5f20-9b14-4c7a-a0e6-71c4b2d95a08

docs.title: Platform resources
docs.text: Create, edit and delete the workspace's resources (links, files and other external references that entries point to) through the Platform API. The Publishing API has no resource routes; published entries carry their resources inline (marvin publish entry <slug> --json | jq .resources).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform resources list
marvin platform resources get <id>
marvin platform resources create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform resources update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform resources delete <id> --yes
marvin platform resources apply-suggestion <id>
marvin platform resources reject-suggestion <id>

Required role

Any member can list and get resources. Create, update, delete, apply-suggestion and reject-suggestion need the workspace EDITOR role. See Workspace roles.

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin. --file <path> is the same as --data @path, and piped stdin works with neither flag.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Lists every resource. Columns: ID, Name, Slug, Type, Description (first 50 characters), URL.

marvin platform resources list
marvin platform resources list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.resourceType == "link") | .slug'

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Shows one resource in full, including suggestionJson when an AI suggestion is pending.

marvin platform resources get 9a40d7c2-1e5b-4a36-8f02-c3b7e6d41a95

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Creates a resource from a JSON body. The required fields are slug, name and resourceType; description, url, externalId, metadata and tag_ids are optional. Prints Created resource: <id> on stderr, then the resource.

marvin platform resources create --data '{
  "slug": "lookbook-pdf",
  "name": "Spring lookbook (PDF)",
  "resourceType": "link",
  "url": "https://example.com/lookbook.pdf"
}'

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Updates a resource with the fields in the JSON body. Prints Updated resource: <id>, then the resource.

marvin platform resources update 9a40… --data '{"name": "Spring lookbook 2026 (PDF)"}'
echo '{"description": "Print-ready"}' | marvin platform resources update 9a40…

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Deletes a resource. Without --yes the command refuses and exits with an error.

Option Description Default --yes Confirm the delete off 
marvin platform resources delete 9a40… --yes

docs.title: apply-suggestion and reject-suggestion
docs.text:
When an AI operation writes back with approval required, its proposed changes are staged on the resource as suggestionJson. apply-suggestion commits them and clears the suggestion; reject-suggestion discards them. Both print the updated resource. See Review queue.

marvin platform resources get 9a40… --json | jq .suggestionJson
marvin platform resources apply-suggestion 9a40…
marvin platform resources reject-suggestion 9a40…

docs.title: Renderers
docs.text: View entry type renderer declarations and capabilities for your workspace.

docs.title: List Renderers
docs.text: marvin publish renderers [options]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Lists entry types with their rendering metadata — renderer name, package, and capabilities (publishable, routable). By default, only entry types with isRendered: true are shown. Use --all to include all entry types.

This command uses the Publishing API (/api/publish/{workspace}/entry-types) via the SDK's renderers.list() method.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Requires a site client token: the --site-token / --token flag, the token saved for the active workspace (marvin workspace token or marvin login --site-token), or the MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN environment variable.

docs.title: marvin publish renderers
docs.text: Option Description Default --all Include entry types without a declared renderer false --json Output as JSON false --yaml Output as YAML false --csv Output as CSV false --output <format> Output format: table, json, yaml, csv table

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
List rendered entry types:

marvin publish renderers

Output:

┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────┬──────────┐
│ Name             │ Slug            │ Renderer   │ Package                          │ Publishable │ Routable │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────┼────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┤
│ Page             │ page            │ page       │ @inneropen/marvin-renderers-core │ yes         │ yes      │
│ Article          │ article         │ article    │ @inneropen/marvin-renderers-core │ yes         │ yes      │
│ FAQ              │ faq             │ faq        │ @inneropen/marvin-renderers-core │ yes         │ yes      │
│ Navigation Item  │ navigation-item │ navigation │ @inneropen/marvin-renderers-core │ yes         │ no       │
└──────────────────┴─────────────────┴────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴─────────────┴──────────┘

Publishable and Routable show yes unless the entry type's capability is explicitly false.

docs.title: Include All Entry Types
docs.text:
marvin publish renderers --all

Shows all entry types, including those without isRendered: true. Non-rendered types will show empty renderer and package columns.

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
marvin publish renderers --json

[
  {
    "name": "Page",
    "slug": "page",
    "isRendered": true,
    "rendering": {
      "renderer": "page",
      "package": "@inneropen/marvin-renderers-core"
    },
    "capabilities": {
      "publishable": true,
      "submittable": false,
      "routable": true
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Human-readable entry type name slug string URL-friendly identifier isRendered boolean Whether this type has a frontend renderer rendering.renderer string Renderer component name (e.g., page, article, faq) rendering.package string npm package providing the renderer rendering.version string Semver range for the required package version rendering.config object Renderer-specific configuration capabilities.publishable boolean Can transition through publishing workflow capabilities.submittable boolean Accepts external data submission capabilities.routable boolean Has its own URL path on the frontend

docs.title: Check Which Renderers a Site Needs
docs.text:
marvin publish renderers --json | jq -r '.[].rendering.renderer'

Output:

page
article
faq
navigation

docs.title: Find Non-Routable Entry Types
docs.text: marvin publish renderers --json | jq '.[] | select(.capabilities.routable == false) | .slug'

docs.title: Count Rendered vs Total Entry Types
docs.text:
echo "Rendered: $(marvin publish renderers --json | jq 'length')"
echo "Total: $(marvin publish renderers --all --json | jq 'length')"

docs.title: Relationship to entry-types
docs.text:
The platform entry-types commands (Platform API) show entry type schemas and field definitions. The publish renderers command (under the Publishing API) focuses on rendering metadata — which renderers are needed and what capabilities each type has.

Command API Focus marvin platform entry-types list Platform Schema, fields, validation marvin publish renderers Publishing Renderer, package, capabilities

docs.title: Related Commands
docs.text:
• marvin platform entry-types list - View entry type schemas (Platform API)
  • marvin publish entries - List entries (can filter by entry type)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This command calls:

GET /api/publish/{workspace}/entry-types

docs.title: Review Queue
docs.text: Work through what's waiting in a workspace: entries by status, AI suggestions that need a yes or no, AI-generated assets awaiting approval, and the dashboard that counts all of it. Plus the scheduling flags on entries update. The commands themselves are documented on Platform entries, Platform assets and Platform resources; this page is the workflow.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform dashboard
marvin platform entries counts
marvin platform entries list [--status <s>[,<s>…]] [--entry-type <slug>] [--suggestions] [--limit <n>]
marvin platform entries apply-suggestion <id>
marvin platform entries reject-suggestion <id>
marvin platform assets apply-suggestion <id>
marvin platform assets reject-suggestion <id>
marvin platform resources apply-suggestion <id>
marvin platform resources reject-suggestion <id>
marvin platform entries suggested-assets list <entry-id>
marvin platform entries suggested-assets approve <entry-id> <asset-id>
marvin platform entries suggested-assets reject <entry-id> <asset-id>
marvin platform entries update <id> [--status <s>] [--publish-at <iso>] [--expire-at <iso>] [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>]

Required role

Any member reads the dashboard, counts and lists. Applying or rejecting an entry's suggestion, approving or rejecting its suggested assets, and updating it follow the entry rules: an AUTHOR for their own drafts, EDITOR for anyone else's entry or to approve, publish or schedule one. Suggestions on assets and resources need EDITOR. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
marvin platform dashboard

Needs attention: 7
┌─────────┬───────────────────┬───────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ (index) │ Item              │ Count │ See it with                                         │
├─────────┼───────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 0       │ Inbox             │ 2     │ marvin platform entries list --status inbox         │
│ 1       │ Drafts            │ 1     │ marvin platform entries list --status draft         │
│ 2       │ Needs review      │ 1     │ marvin platform entries list --status needs_review  │
│ 3       │ AI suggestions    │ 3     │ marvin platform entries list --suggestions          │
│ 4       │ Failures (7 days) │ 0     │                                                     │
└─────────┴───────────────────┴───────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Recent activity
…

The See it with column names the command that works through each count, and stays empty when the count is zero. Recent activity has the columns When, Event, Message and Entity.

AI suggestions counts entries, assets and resources with a pending suggestion. Failures counts failed scheduled-task runs, webhook deliveries and AI executions in the last 7 days. With --json you get the API's {attention: {inbox, drafts, needsReview, aiSuggestions, failures}, recentActivity: [...]}.

docs.title: Counts and filtered lists
docs.text:
See entries list and entries counts.

marvin platform entries counts            # every status, zero-filled, plus total
marvin platform entries counts --json     # {"inbox": 2, "draft": 1, …, "total": 48}

entries list returns entries newest first. The API has no filters, so the CLI fetches the list and filters it:

Option Keeps --status <s> Entries with this status; comma-separate several (inbox,needs_review) --entry-type <slug> Entries of this type (slug or id) --suggestions Entries with a pending AI suggestion (suggestionJson set) --limit <n> The first n after filtering 
marvin platform entries list --status needs_review --entry-type post
marvin platform entries list --suggestions --json | jq -r '.[].id'

docs.title: AI suggestions
docs.text:
When an AI operation writes back with approval required, its proposed changes are staged on the item as suggestionJson instead of being applied. Look at it with get, then apply or discard it:

marvin platform entries get 6f1c… --json | jq .suggestionJson
marvin platform entries apply-suggestion 6f1c…     # commits the changes and clears the suggestion
marvin platform entries reject-suggestion 6f1c…    # clears it without applying

assets and resources have the same two commands (they need EDITOR). Each prints the updated item.

Approve every pending entry suggestion in one go:

marvin platform entries list --suggestions --json | jq -r '.[].id' |
  xargs -n1 marvin platform entries apply-suggestion

docs.title: Suggested assets
docs.text:
An AI media operation (e.g. background removal) can attach the asset it made to the entry as a suggestion: it stays out of published output until someone approves it.

marvin platform entries suggested-assets list <entry-id>       # ID, Slug, Name, Type, Operation, Derived from
marvin platform entries suggested-assets approve <entry-id> <asset-id>
marvin platform entries suggested-assets reject <entry-id> <asset-id>

Approving makes it a normal attached asset. Rejecting unlinks it, and deletes the asset if nothing else uses it.

docs.title: Scheduling and status
docs.text:
entries update takes --status, --publish-at and --expire-at, so you can schedule without writing a JSON body:

marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --publish-at 2026-10-31T09:00:00Z
marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --expire-at 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --publish-at ""          # clear the schedule ("none" works too)
marvin platform entries update 6f1c… --status needs_review

Times are ISO 8601; the CLI rejects one it can't read before calling the API. The flags combine with --data (or --file), and win over the same field in it (publish_at or publishAt). With only flags, the command doesn't wait on stdin for a body. Full options: entries update.

docs.title: Scheduled Tasks
docs.text: Scheduled tasks run built-in maintenance jobs for the workspace on a schedule: an interval, a cron expression, or once. These commands create and edit them, trigger a run on demand, and read their execution history.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks list [--enabled-only] [--failed-only]
marvin platform scheduled-tasks get <id-or-slug>
marvin platform scheduled-tasks create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform scheduled-tasks update <id-or-slug> [--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>] [--enable | --disable]
marvin platform scheduled-tasks delete <id-or-slug> --yes
marvin platform scheduled-tasks run <id-or-slug>
marvin platform scheduled-tasks history <id-or-slug> [--limit <n>] [--failed-only]
marvin platform scheduled-tasks types [--detailed]
marvin platform scheduled-tasks log [--limit <n>]
marvin platform scheduled-tasks stats

platform tasks is an alias for platform scheduled-tasks, and execute is an alias for run.

Required role

Every scheduled-task command except types, reads included, needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

Commands that take <id-or-slug> accept either the task's id or its slug. --data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path.

docs.title: The task object
docs.text:
Field Description name Task name (required) description Free text task_type What the task does; marvin platform scheduled-tasks types lists them (required) schedule_type cron, interval or once (required) schedule_config Settings for the schedule type, for example {"interval_seconds": 86400} (required) task_config Settings for the task type; types --detailed shows each type's config schema enabled Whether the task runs retry_policy Retry settings, optional

Without --data or --file, create prints an example body and exits 1.

docs.title: List, get, stats
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks list
marvin platform scheduled-tasks list --failed-only
marvin platform scheduled-tasks get daily-cleanup
marvin platform scheduled-tasks stats
Option (list) Description --enabled-only Show only enabled tasks --failed-only Show only tasks whose last status is failed

Columns: id, name, task_type, schedule_type, enabled, last_status, next_run_at.

stats counts the workspace's tasks: total, enabled, disabled, never run, and how many last succeeded or failed. Table output is a short summary (with a hint to run list --failed-only when any failed); --json gives {total, enabled, disabled, never_run, failed, success}.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks create --data '{
  "name": "Daily Cleanup",
  "description": "Clean up old files",
  "task_type": "cleanup_temp_files",
  "schedule_type": "interval",
  "schedule_config": {"interval_seconds": 86400},
  "task_config": {"age_hours": 24},
  "enabled": true
}'

Prints Created scheduled task: <id> on stderr and the task on stdout.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks update daily-cleanup --disable
marvin platform scheduled-tasks update daily-cleanup --data '{"schedule_config": {"interval_seconds": 43200}}'
Option Description --data, --file Fields to change --enable Set enabled to true (applied after --data; wins over it) --disable Set enabled to false

With none of the four options the command exits 1.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks delete daily-cleanup --yes

--yes is required; without it the command exits 1. With --json it prints {"deleted": "<id-or-slug>"}.

docs.title: Run now
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks run daily-cleanup

Triggers the task immediately, bypassing its schedule, and returns once the run is triggered (Task execution triggered, with {"ok": true, "task": "<id-or-slug>"} under --json). Read the outcome with history.

docs.title: History and log
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks history daily-cleanup --limit 10
marvin platform scheduled-tasks history daily-cleanup --failed-only
marvin platform scheduled-tasks log --limit 100

history shows one task's executions; log shows executions of every task in the workspace.

Option Description Default --limit <number> Records to fetch (history: "Number of records to show"; log: maximum entries) 50 --failed-only history only: keep failed executions. Applied after --limit, so it filters those records off

history columns: executed_at, status, duration_ms, error_message, retry_attempt. log columns: executed_at, task_id, status, duration_ms, error_message. An empty result prints No execution history found / No execution log entries found in table mode.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
marvin platform scheduled-tasks types
marvin platform scheduled-tasks types --detailed --json
Option Description --detailed Show detailed metadata including config schemas

Without --detailed, table output is a list of task type names and --json an array of names. With it, a table of task_type, name, description; --json adds each type's config_schema. Any member can run types.

docs.title: Secrets and Variables
docs.text:
Secrets and variables are named workspace values that other configuration refers to by slug with {{SLUG}} placeholders (for example in integration action arguments), so credentials and per-environment settings stay out of the definitions that use them.

  • Secrets are write-only: the value is encrypted when stored and no read command returns it, apart from the explicit reveal.
  • Variables are plain-text key/value config; list shows their values.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform secrets list
marvin platform secrets slugs
marvin platform secrets reveal <id>
marvin platform secrets create --name <name> [--value-stdin | --value <value>] [--slug <slug>] [--description <text>]
marvin platform secrets update <id> [--name <name>] [--value-stdin | --value <value>] [--description <text>]
marvin platform secrets delete <id> --yes

marvin platform variables list
marvin platform variables create --name <name> --value <value> [--slug <slug>] [--description <text>]
marvin platform variables update <id> [--name <name>] [--value <value>] [--description <text>]
marvin platform variables delete <id> --yes

Required role

Creating, updating, deleting and revealing a secret needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role; secrets list and secrets slugs carry no role requirement in the CLI. Every variables command, reads included, needs ADMIN. See Workspace roles.

<id> is the UUID shown in the ID column of list.

docs.title: Slugs
docs.text: create takes --slug, or derives it from --name when omitted. Either way the CLI normalises it before sending: upper-cased, with every run of characters other than A-Z and 0-9 replaced by _ ("Stripe key" becomes STRIPE_KEY). Use it as {{STRIPE_KEY}}. A slug cannot be changed by update.

docs.title: List and slugs
docs.text:
marvin platform secrets list
marvin platform secrets slugs

list shows metadata only (ID, Name, Slug, Description); values are never returned. slugs prints the slugs available for {{SLUG}} interpolation, one per line (a JSON array with --json).

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
pass show stripe/live | marvin platform secrets create --name "Stripe key" --value-stdin --description "Live API key"
marvin platform secrets create --name "Webhook signing secret"       # prompts for the value, hidden
Option Description Default --name <name> Secret name (required) --value-stdin Read the value from stdin --value <value> The value on the command line (deprecated) --slug <slug> Slug for {{SLUG}} interpolation derived from --name --description <description> Description none

How the value is supplied, in order:

  1. --value-stdin reads it from a pipe (surrounding whitespace is trimmed; an empty value is an error).
  2. --value is accepted but prints a warning, because the secret lands in your shell history. Giving both --value and --value-stdin is an error.
  3. With neither, an interactive terminal prompts for it with the input hidden. Without a terminal the command fails with No secret value: pipe it in with --value-stdin.

Prints Created secret: <id> on stderr and the secret's metadata (no value) on stdout.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
marvin platform secrets update 8a41f6d2-0c93-47be-9d15-6e2b7f3a1c40 --description "Rotated 2026-10"
cat new-key.txt | marvin platform secrets update 8a41f6d2-0c93-47be-9d15-6e2b7f3a1c40 --value-stdin

Changes the name, description and/or value; only what you pass is sent. --value-stdin and --value behave as for create, except that no prompt appears: without either, the value is left alone. With nothing to change the command exits 1 (Provide at least one of --name, --value-stdin, or --description).

docs.title: Reveal
docs.text:
marvin platform secrets reveal 8a41f6d2-0c93-47be-9d15-6e2b7f3a1c40
marvin platform secrets reveal 8a41f6d2-0c93-47be-9d15-6e2b7f3a1c40 --json | jq -r .value

Prints the plaintext value, as {"value": "..."} data on stdout (so it ends up in whatever captures the output). It is the only command that returns a secret's value.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin platform secrets delete 8a41f6d2-0c93-47be-9d15-6e2b7f3a1c40 --yes

--yes is required; without it the command exits 1. With --json it prints {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
marvin platform variables list
marvin platform variables create --name "Site URL" --value https://example.com --description "Public base URL"
marvin platform variables update 3d9c7a05-f1e2-4b68-a0c4-85e6d2b19f73 --value https://www.example.com
marvin platform variables delete 3d9c7a05-f1e2-4b68-a0c4-85e6d2b19f73 --yes

list columns: ID, Name, Slug, Value, Description.

Option Applies to Description --name <name> create (required), update Variable name --value <value> create (required), update Variable value --slug <slug> create Slug for {{SLUG}} interpolation; derived from --name when omitted (see Slugs) --description <description> create, update Description --yes delete Skip confirmation prompt (required; without it the command exits 1)

create prints Created variable: <id> on stderr and the variable on stdout; update only sends the fields you pass (a non-empty --name or --value, or any --description) and exits 1 if there are none.

docs.title: Site Rebuild
docs.text:
Ask Marvin to rebuild the workspace's static site, and see where the rebuild stands. These are Platform API commands (user token); the read-only site configuration is marvin publish site.

Required role

Both commands need the workspace EDITOR role or above — the same role that publishes. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403).

Server requirement

POST/GET /api/platform/site/rebuild is new: the server needs a Marvin release that includes the site rebuild endpoint (newer than rc.198). An older server answers 404.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform site rebuild [--reason <text>]
marvin platform site rebuild-status

docs.title: How a rebuild is sent
docs.text:
Marvin doesn't build the site itself. A rebuild goes to whatever the workspace has set up to build it, on the Webhook Triggered event: an outgoing webhook (your host's deploy hook), or an integration action subscribed to that event (for example Cloudflare Pages → Deploy).

Rebuild requests coalesce. A request joins the workspace's pending rebuild if there is one, and the pending rebuild is sent once requests have been quiet for the server's SITE_REBUILD_QUIET_SECONDS (and no later than its maximum wait after the first request). Calling site rebuild ten times in a minute costs one build.

docs.title: Request a rebuild
docs.text:
marvin platform site rebuild
marvin platform site rebuild --reason "Nightly content sync"
Option Description Default --reason <text> Why, for the build log (at most 200 characters) "Rebuild requested by "

Table mode prints the outcome on stderr:

✓ Rebuild queued (joins 1 earlier request(s)): sends at 2026-10-05T10:01:05Z
  via Pages (integration: cloudflare_pages → deploy)
  reason: Nightly content sync

With --json, stdout gets:

{
  "ok": true,
  "requested": true,
  "queuedAt": "2026-10-05T10:00:00Z",
  "lastRequestedAt": "2026-10-05T10:00:05Z",
  "expectedSendAt": "2026-10-05T10:01:05Z",
  "requestCount": 2,
  "reason": "Nightly content sync",
  "target": null,
  "targets": [
    { "kind": "integration", "id": "…", "name": "Pages", "provider": "cloudflare_pages", "action": "deploy" }
  ]
}

requestCount above 1 means the request joined a pending rebuild; queuedAt stays the first request's time. When nothing is set up to build the site the server answers 409 with what to configure, nothing is queued, and the command exits 1.

docs.title: Rebuild status
docs.text:
marvin platform site rebuild-status
marvin platform site rebuild-status --json

Takes no options. In table mode it prints:

Configured:  yes
Builds via:  Deploy hook (webhook)
Quiet time:  60s (sent at most 600s after the first request)
Pending:     none
Last sent:   2026-10-05T09:00:00Z — Rebuild requested by Jo
Last build:  deployment completed at 2026-10-05T09:02:00Z — Deployed

The JSON has configured, target/targets, quietSeconds, maxWaitSeconds, pending (the queued rebuild: request count, first and last request, expected send time, reason, the changes it covers), lastSent (the last Webhook Triggered event) and lastBuild (the newest site_build_* / site_deployment_* status a host reported back), each null when there is none.

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
# Rebuild after an import, and fail the job if nothing builds the site
marvin workspace import --file bundle.zip
marvin platform site rebuild --reason "Import from staging" --json | jq -r .expectedSendAt

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Command Endpoint rebuild POST /api/platform/site/rebuild (202) rebuild-status GET /api/platform/site/rebuild

docs.title: Site Configuration
docs.text: Fetch the workspace's public site configuration (title, tagline, logo, locale, SEO and so on) from the Publishing API.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
marvin publish site

The command takes no options of its own. It uses the publish group options --site-token <token> (alias --token) plus the global options.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
marvin publish site prints one object with two parts: workspace (slug, name) and site. In the default table mode the object is pretty-printed rather than drawn as a table; use --json, --yaml or --csv for machine-readable output.

marvin publish site --json

{
  "workspace": { "slug": "acme", "name": "Acme" },
  "site": {
    "title": "My Awesome Site",
    "tagline": "Built with Marvin CMS",
    "description": "A modern headless CMS solution",
    "canonicalUrl": "https://example.com",
    "logo": "https://cdn.example.com/logo.png",
    "favicon": "https://cdn.example.com/favicon.ico",
    "locale": "en-US",
    "timezone": "America/New_York",
    "contactEmail": "hello@example.com",
    "social": {},
    "seo": { "robots": "index,follow", "ogType": "website" },
    "metadataJson": {}
  }
}
site field Description title, tagline, description Public identity of the site canonicalUrl Canonical base URL logo, favicon Image URLs locale Locale (default en-US) timezone IANA timezone (default America/New_York) contactEmail Public contact address social Social links map seo Site-wide SEO defaults (title template, keywords, robots, Open Graph type, and similar) metadataJson Free-form metadata

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Site title
marvin publish site --json | jq -r '.site.title'

# Save the configuration
marvin publish site --json > site-config.json

# Confirm which workspace the token belongs to
marvin publish site --json | jq -r '.workspace.slug'

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Needs a site client token. It is resolved in this order: --site-token / --token flag, the token saved for the active workspace (marvin workspace token, or marvin login --site-token), then the MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN environment variable. The API URL comes from --api-url, the saved credentials or MARVIN_API_URL.

export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token
marvin publish site --site-token marvin_sk_your_token

A 401 means the token is invalid or missing; a 404 usually means the workspace slug or API URL is wrong (check marvin workspace current).

docs.title: Related Commands
docs.text:
• marvin publish entries - List published entries
  • marvin publish collections - List collections
  • marvin workspace token - Save a site client token

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This command calls GET /api/publish/{workspace}/site. See API Mapping.

docs.title: Smart Collections
docs.text: A smart collection's members come from rules — entry types, statuses, tags and the like — and the server keeps its membership up to date as content changes. Preview rules before saving them, create or change a collection's rules, see who's in it, and set the order collections are listed in.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform collections preview --rules <json|@file|-> [--target-type entry|asset|resource] [--limit <n>]
marvin platform collections create --data <json|@file|-> [--smart-rules <json|@file|->]
marvin platform collections update <id> [--smart-rules <json|@file|->] [--data <json|@file|->]
marvin platform collections members <id>
marvin platform collections order <id> [<id>…]
marvin platform collections order --data '[{"id": "…", "sortOrder": 0}, …]'

Required role

preview, create, update and order need the workspace EDITOR role; any member lists members. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: Preview rules
docs.text:
marvin platform collections preview --rules '{"tags": ["news"], "statuses": ["published"]}'

Matching entries: 12 (showing 10)
┌─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
│ (index) │ ID       │ Type    │ Label        │ Slug         │
…

Nothing is saved. The rules are evaluated by the same code that fills the collection on save, so the count is exactly what the collection would hold. --limit (default 10, at most 50) caps the listed matches; the total counts them all. --target-type picks what the rules select (entry by default). Rules this target type doesn't read are listed as ignored; an empty rule set matches nothing, and the command says so.

--rules takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin. With --json you get {total, items: [{id, label, slug, type}], ignoredKeys, note}.

docs.title: Create or change a smart collection
docs.text:
marvin platform collections create --data '{"name": "News"}' --smart-rules '{"tags": ["news"]}'
marvin platform collections update 3c9e… --smart-rules @rules.json

--smart-rules sets the collection's rules and makes it smart (isSmart: true). On update it needs no --data; with --data too, --smart-rules wins over any smartRules in the body. Don't add or reorder entries on a smart collection by hand: the rules own its membership.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
marvin platform collections members 3c9e…

Columns: ID, Type, Label (the entry's title or the asset's or resource's name), Slug — the same for entry, asset and resource collections. (collections entries <id> still lists an entry collection's entries in their collection order, with every entry field.)

docs.title: Order collections
docs.text:
marvin platform collections order 3c9e… 7a21… 0f4d…         # in this order (sortOrder 0, 1, 2)
marvin platform collections order --data @order.json        # [{"id": "…", "sortOrder": 10}, …]

Sets the order collections are listed in, system collections included. Ids that don't belong to a collection in this workspace are skipped; the command says how many. With --json it prints {"ok": true, "updated": <n>}.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: • Platform Collections - every platform collections command, including list, get, delete, entries, reorder and update-entry

docs.title: Health & Version
docs.text: Two utility commands that need no sign-in: check that a Marvin API is reachable, and print the version of the CLI itself. For server-side details (server version, configuration, statistics) use Admin system.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin system health
marvin system version

Neither takes options beyond the global options.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
marvin system health
marvin system health --api-url https://marvin.example.com
marvin system health --json

Calls the API's public health endpoint, with no token. The API URL comes from --api-url or the MARVIN_API_URL environment variable; if neither is set the command exits 1 with an error.

On success it prints API is healthy, the URL it checked and whatever the endpoint returned. With --json or --yaml the output is a single object:

{ "healthy": true, "url": "https://marvin.example.com", "response": null }

response holds the endpoint's reply, or null when it sends none. When the API cannot be reached the command prints Failed to reach API with the error and exits 1, so it works as a script gate:

marvin system health --api-url "$MARVIN_API_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Marvin is down"; exit 1; }

docs.title: Version
docs.text:
marvin system version
marvin system version --json

Prints Marvin CLI v<version>, or {"version": "<version>"} with --json or --yaml. This is the installed CLI's version, not the server's; the server's is in marvin admin system info.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Tags are the workspace's shared labels. Entries, assets and resources carry them; smart-collection rules and the publishing API's --tag filter match on their slugs.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform tags list
marvin platform tags get <tag>
marvin platform tags create (--name <name> [--slug <slug>] [--color <color>] | --data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform tags update <tag> (--name <name> | --color <color> | --data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform tags delete <tag> --yes
marvin platform tags attach <tag> (--entry <id> | --asset <id> | --resource <id>)
marvin platform tags detach <tag> (--entry <id> | --asset <id> | --resource <id>)

Every command that takes <tag> accepts its id or its slug.

Required role

Any member lists tags. An AUTHOR creates tags and tags their own draft entries. Renaming or deleting a tag, and tagging anyone else's entry, an asset or a resource, needs EDITOR. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
marvin platform tags list

Columns: ID, Slug, Name, Color, Entries (entries carrying the tag), Uses (entries, assets and resources together).

docs.title: Create, rename, delete
docs.text:
--data takes {name, slug?, color?} ({name?, color?} for update) as inline JSON, @path or - for stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path. Without --data/--file, create needs --name and update needs --name or --color. delete refuses without --yes.

marvin platform tags create --name "Chore Coat"            # slug: chore-coat
marvin platform tags create --name "News" --color "#FF5733"
marvin platform tags update chore-coat --name "Chore coats"
marvin platform tags delete chore-coat --yes

create is find-or-create by slug: creating a tag whose slug already exists returns the existing tag, so a script can call it without checking first. A tag's slug never changes; update renames or recolors it. Deleting a tag removes it from everything that carried it.

docs.title: Tag and untag
docs.text:
marvin platform tags attach news --entry 6f1c…
marvin platform tags attach news --asset 2b7e…
marvin platform tags detach news --resource 9a40…

Name exactly one target (--entry, --asset or --resource); naming none or several is an error. Attaching is idempotent. With --json the result is {"ok": true, "tagId": "…", "entryId": "…", "attached": true} (or assetId/resourceId, detached).

Tag everything a query finds:

marvin platform entries list --status published --entry-type post --json | jq -r '.[].id' |
  xargs -I{} marvin platform tags attach news --entry {}

docs.title: User Account
docs.text: Self-service commands for the signed-in user: view and edit your profile, manage personal API tokens and change your password. They act on your own account only; to manage other people's accounts see Admin users.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin user profile show
marvin user profile update (--full-name <name> | --username <username> | --email <email>)
marvin user tokens list
marvin user tokens create --name <name> [--description <text>]
marvin user tokens get <token-id>
marvin user tokens update <token-id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin user tokens revoke <token-id>
marvin user tokens rotate <token-id>
marvin user tokens delete <token-id>
marvin user change-password

These need a signed-in user (marvin login) but no particular role.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
marvin user profile show
marvin user profile update --full-name "Sam Rivera"
marvin user profile update --username sam
marvin user profile update --email sam@example.com

show prints your user record: id, username, fullName, email, authMethod, platformRole, group and workspaceMemberships.

Option Description Default --full-name <name> New display name (sent as fullName) unchanged --name <name> Alias for --full-name unchanged --username <username> New username unchanged --email <email> New email address unchanged

update needs at least one option; with neither it exits 1 with Provide at least one of --full-name, --username or --email. It prints Profile updated, or {"ok": true, "updated": {...}} with --json.

docs.title: Personal API tokens
docs.text:
A personal API token lets scripts call the platform API as you, as you, where an interactive login is not possible. Credentials for an application rather than a person are API clients.

The token value is shown once

create and rotate print the token value once, with a warning on stderr (Save this token now - it will not be shown again!). Store it in a secret manager straight away; list and get never show it.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin user tokens list
marvin user tokens get 8c4e1f09-3b72-4d65-a1f8-0e9d7c2b5a36

list columns: id, name, description, createdAt, lastUsedAt, enabled. get prints one token record: id, userId, name, description, enabled, lastUsedAt, revokedAt, integrationId and timestamps.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
marvin user tokens create --name ci-deploy --description "Nightly publish job"
marvin user tokens create --name ci-deploy --json | jq -r '.token'
Option Description Default -n, --name <name> Token name (required) -d, --description <description> Token description none

The output is the new token record, including token (the secret value). Personal API tokens have no expiry in the Marvin API, so there is no --expires option; revoke a token with user tokens revoke when it is no longer needed.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
marvin user tokens update 8c4e1f09-3b72-4d65-a1f8-0e9d7c2b5a36 --data '{"description": "Nightly publish"}'
marvin user tokens update 8c4e1f09-3b72-4d65-a1f8-0e9d7c2b5a36 --data '{"enabled": false}'
Option Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> Token data as inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin none --file <path> JSON file with the token data (same as --data @path; - for stdin) none

The payload may contain name, description and enabled; setting enabled to false turns the token off without revoking it. Prints Updated API token: <id> and the token record.

docs.title: Revoke, rotate, delete
docs.text:
marvin user tokens revoke 8c4e1f09-3b72-4d65-a1f8-0e9d7c2b5a36
marvin user tokens rotate 8c4e1f09-3b72-4d65-a1f8-0e9d7c2b5a36
marvin user tokens delete 8c4e1f09-3b72-4d65-a1f8-0e9d7c2b5a36
  • revoke invalidates the token. Prints Token <id> revoked successfully, or {"deleted": "<id>"} with --json.
  • rotate revokes the token and creates a replacement in one step, and prints the new record including its new token value. Update whatever used the old token.
  • delete removes the token record. Prints Token <id> deleted successfully, or {"deleted": "<id>"}.

None of the three asks for confirmation.

docs.title: Change password
docs.text:
marvin user change-password

Prompts for your current password, the new password and a confirmation, with input hidden, so nothing lands in shell history or the process list. There are no flags; it needs an interactive terminal. It exits 1 if either value is empty or the two new passwords differ, and prints Password changed successfully on success.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: Webhooks are the workspace's outgoing HTTP calls: Marvin sends a request to a URL when an event happens or at a scheduled time. These commands manage the webhook definitions and read their delivery logs. For webhooks Marvin receives, see Incoming webhooks.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform webhooks list [--page <n>] [--per-page <n>] [--all]
marvin platform webhooks get <id>
marvin platform webhooks create (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform webhooks update <id> (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform webhooks delete <id> --yes
marvin platform webhooks test <id>
marvin platform webhooks types
marvin platform webhooks rerun
marvin platform webhooks log [--limit <n>]
marvin platform webhooks logs <id> [--limit <n>]

Required role

Every webhook command except types, reads included, needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin; --file <path> is the same as --data @path. With neither, create and update read piped stdin.

docs.title: The webhook object
docs.text:
Field Description Default name Webhook name (required) url Target URL (required) method GET or POST POST webhookType When it fires and what it sends: generic, user, entries, event_driven, workflow. marvin platform webhooks types lists what the server offers generic enabled Whether the webhook fires true scheduledTime Time of day for scheduled types none headers Extra request headers, an object of strings none subscribedEvents Event types an event_driven webhook listens for none customPayload Object sent as the body instead of the default payload none

update sends the whole body to the server, so include name and url again along with the fields you change. Fetch the current definition with get --json to start from.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform webhooks list
marvin platform webhooks get 3f2a9c10-4b7e-4c55-9a1d-2e6f0b8d7a11 --json

list shows one page (50 by default); --all fetches every page and ignores --page.

Option Description Default --page <number> Page number 1 --per-page <number> Items per page 50 --all Fetch every page off

Columns: ID, Name, URL, Method, Enabled.

docs.title: Create and update
docs.text:
marvin platform webhooks create --data '{
  "name": "Rebuild site",
  "url": "https://hooks.example.com/rebuild",
  "webhookType": "event_driven",
  "subscribedEvents": ["entry_published"],
  "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer abc123"}
}'

marvin platform webhooks update 3f2a9c10-4b7e-4c55-9a1d-2e6f0b8d7a11 --file rebuild.json

Both print Created webhook: <id> / Updated webhook: <id> on stderr and the webhook on stdout.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
marvin platform webhooks delete 3f2a9c10-4b7e-4c55-9a1d-2e6f0b8d7a11 --yes

--yes is required; without it the command exits 1 with Delete requires --yes confirmation flag. With --json the result is {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Test, rerun and types
docs.text:
marvin platform webhooks test 3f2a9c10-4b7e-4c55-9a1d-2e6f0b8d7a11
marvin platform webhooks rerun
marvin platform webhooks types
  • test schedules a test delivery and returns at once (Webhook test scheduled); read the outcome with logs <id>.
  • rerun re-fires today's scheduled webhooks (everything due since 00:00 UTC) in the background and prints the server's message and Requeued: <n> webhooks.
  • types prints the webhook types the server supports.

docs.title: Delivery logs
docs.text:
marvin platform webhooks log --limit 20
marvin platform webhooks logs 3f2a9c10-4b7e-4c55-9a1d-2e6f0b8d7a11 --json | jq '.[] | {status, httpStatusCode, errorMessage}'

log covers every webhook in the workspace; logs <id> one webhook.

Option Description Default --limit <number> Maximum number of entries to return 50

Columns: ID, Webhook (id), Status, HTTP (status code), Executed. --json also carries errorMessage, retryAttempt, requestPayload and responseBody.

docs.title: Workers
docs.text: Workers run heavy jobs (ffmpeg, PDFs, anything that does not belong in the API) as a runner, a dispatcher, a container or a Kubernetes Job. They read and write three kinds of record by slug: job, job-kind and worker. Core ships them as the Workers blueprints; workers setup adds whichever the workspace is missing.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform workers setup

Required role

setup changes workspace structure and needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role.

docs.title: setup
docs.text:
marvin platform workers setup
marvin platform workers setup --json

It is marvin platform blueprints apply job job-kind worker --source core with the next steps said aloud. It creates what is missing and never overwrites what exists, so a workspace that already has a job type of its own keeps it, and running setup twice changes nothing. The second run says the workspace is already set up.

Then make a token that can reach only this workspace and start a worker with it:

marvin user tokens create --name worker --pin <workspace-slug>

A worker authenticates with that token (MARVIN_USER_TOKEN) and the API address (MARVIN_API_URL); Settings -> Workers in the web app shows the commands for a process, Docker, Podman and Kubernetes.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
Manage the workspace's workflows: a trigger, optional conditions and target query, and a list of actions that run on an event, on a schedule, or on demand. The API and the SDK call them automations; the CLI uses the manual's name, and marvin platform automations works as an alias.

Required role

Every workflow command, reads included, needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

Every command that takes <workflow> accepts the workflow's id or its slug.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows list
marvin platform workflows get <workflow>
marvin platform workflows options
marvin platform workflows create --data <json|@file|->
marvin platform workflows update <workflow> --data <json|@file|->
marvin platform workflows delete <workflow> --yes
marvin platform workflows enable <workflow>
marvin platform workflows disable <workflow>
marvin platform workflows validate [workflow] [--data <json|@file|->]
marvin platform workflows preview [workflow] [--data <json|@file|->] [--payload <json>]
marvin platform workflows run <workflow> [--dry-run] [--entry-id <id> | --event-id <id>]
marvin platform workflows samples <workflow> [--limit <n>]
marvin platform workflows executions <workflow> [--status <status>] [--limit <n>]
marvin platform workflows execution <workflow> <execution-id>

--data takes inline JSON, @path to read a file, or - to read stdin. --file <path> is the same as --data @path.

docs.title: The definition
docs.text:
A workflow is {name, slug?, enabled?, definition}. The definition has four parts:

Part What it does trigger When it runs: type is one of event, manual, schedule, chained, on_error, incoming_webhook, mcp; an event trigger also names the event (e.g. entry_published) target Optional. A query ({"entity": "entry", "query": {...}}) that selects the entities to act on; without one the actions run on whatever the trigger handed over conditions Optional. {field, op, value} checks (ops: eq, neq, contains, in, starts_with, exists, changed, changed_from, changed_to), combinable with all / any / not actions The steps, in order. kind is one of the registered executors (operation, integration, webhook, entry, emit_event, handler)

options prints the full vocabulary the server accepts.

Example, tag-new-posts.json:

{
  "name": "Tag new posts",
  "slug": "tag-new-posts",
  "definition": {
    "trigger": { "type": "event", "event": "entry_published" },
    "conditions": [{ "field": "entry.entry_type", "op": "eq", "value": "post" }],
    "actions": [{ "kind": "operation", "op": "generate_tags", "write_back": true }]
  }
}

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows options --json | jq '.triggerTypes'

Prints the full vocabulary the server accepts when building a definition: trigger types, condition fields per trigger, action kinds, AI operations, webhooks, and the definition's JSON schema. The output is structured data, so it is most useful with --json or --yaml. It takes no options.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows list

Columns: ID, Slug, Name, Enabled, Trigger (type and event/schedule), Steps (number of actions).

marvin platform workflows get tag-new-posts --json

Prints the workflow with its full definition. <workflow> is the workflow's id or slug.

docs.title: Create, update, delete
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows create --data @tag-new-posts.json
marvin platform workflows update tag-new-posts --data '{"name":"Tag published posts"}'
marvin platform workflows delete tag-new-posts --yes
Command Argument Description update, delete <workflow> Workflow id or slug Option Applies to Description Default --data <json\|@file\|-> create, update The workflow (create) or the fields to change (update) as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> create, update JSON file with the same (same as --data @path) --yes delete Confirm the delete; the command refuses to run without it

A workflow is created disabled unless the body sets "enabled": true; the ✓ line on stderr says so. update takes any of name, enabled and definition. delete needs --yes and prints {"deleted": "<id>"} in JSON mode.

docs.title: Enable and disable
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows enable tag-new-posts
marvin platform workflows disable tag-new-posts

A disabled workflow's trigger doesn't fire, and run refuses it (a dry run still works). Both print the updated workflow.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows validate tag-new-posts            # the saved definition
marvin platform workflows validate --data @definition.json  # a definition, or a workflow body with one
Argument / option Description Default [workflow] Workflow id or slug whose saved definition to check; omit it when passing --data --data <json\|@file\|-> A definition (or a workflow body with one) as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with a definition (same as --data @path)

An advisory check for steps that use data the trigger doesn't provide, such as entry.* conditions under a webhook trigger. The server never rejects the definition; it returns issues, each with a level (warning or error), where (trigger, condition, action), index and message.

The command exits 1 when any issue has level error, so it can gate a CI job:

marvin platform workflows validate --data @workflows/tag-new-posts.json --json

docs.title: Preview
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows preview nightly-cleanup
marvin platform workflows preview --data @definition.json --payload '{"slug":"hello"}'
Argument / option Description Default [workflow] Workflow id or slug whose saved definition to preview; omit it when passing --data --data <json\|@file\|-> A definition (or a workflow body with one) as JSON, @path to read a file, or - for stdin --file <path> JSON file with a definition (same as --data @path) --payload <json> Test payload for the target query, as JSON

Resolves the definition's target query (with an optional test payload for $event.* values) and shows which entities it would act on, without running anything. The result has total (the full match count), capped (the run is limited to the first 250), and matches (the capped set that also passes the conditions). A definition without a target query has nothing to preview.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows run tag-new-posts                      # run now
marvin platform workflows run tag-new-posts --dry-run            # what it would do
marvin platform workflows run tag-new-posts --dry-run --entry-id <entry-id>
marvin platform workflows run tag-new-posts --dry-run --event-id <event-id>
Argument / option Description Default <workflow> Workflow id or slug --dry-run Resolve every step's inputs but execute and record nothing (works on a disabled workflow) --entry-id <id> With --dry-run: test against this entry's latest event --event-id <id> With --dry-run: test against this event

A real run is the Manual trigger: it skips the trigger and the conditions and runs the actions now. It prints {"ok": ..., "status": "ran", "ran": <targets>, "result": {...}} in JSON mode and exits 1 when the run isn't ok. A disabled workflow can't be run (409).

--dry-run evaluates the target and conditions and resolves each action's inputs, but executes nothing (no AI call, no change, no webhook POST) and records nothing. It works on a disabled workflow. The result's plan lists each step with its resolved inputs and status (success = would run, failed = a gate or resolve error stopped it).

An event-triggered workflow is dry-run against a sample event. By default the server uses the latest matching event; --entry-id tests against that entry's latest event of the trigger's type (or one built for it), --event-id against a specific event-log row. The result then also says whether the trigger matched, whether the conditions pass, and whether a real run would fire. --entry-id and --event-id only apply with --dry-run, and only one at a time.

docs.title: Samples
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows samples tag-new-posts --limit 5
Argument / option Description Default <workflow> Workflow id or slug --limit <number> How many samples 10

The events (and, for entry triggers, recent entries no event covers) a dry run can test against, newest first, with whether each passes the conditions. Pass an id from here to run --dry-run --event-id or --entry-id.

docs.title: Run history
docs.text:
marvin platform workflows executions tag-new-posts                 # alias: runs
marvin platform workflows executions tag-new-posts --status failed --limit 50
Argument / option Description Default <workflow> Workflow id or slug --status <status> Only runs with this status: running, success, partial, failed or handled --limit <number> How many recent runs to fetch 20

Recent runs, newest first: status, trigger, start time, duration, targets run/matched, steps ok/total, error. --limit (default 20) is how many runs to fetch; --status filters those: running, success, partial, failed, or handled (runs whose failures the integration error policy took care of). The API has no status filter, so --limit counts before filtering.

marvin platform workflows execution tag-new-posts <execution-id>   # alias: run-detail

Takes the workflow (id or slug) and the run's id (the ID column of executions); no options. One run in full. In table mode: a summary (status, trigger, timing, targets, step counts, the run it retried, the error), a table of per-step records with how the error policy handled each failure, the retry chain (earlier runs this one retries), and any integration retries still queued. --json prints the API's record, including actions, retryChain, retries and definitionSnapshot.

docs.title: Walkthrough: dry run, then enable
docs.text:
# 1. Create it (disabled)
marvin platform workflows create --data @tag-new-posts.json

# 2. Check the definition makes sense for its trigger
marvin platform workflows validate tag-new-posts

# 3. Pick a sample event and see what a run would do
marvin platform workflows samples tag-new-posts
marvin platform workflows run tag-new-posts --dry-run --event-id <event-id>

# 4. Turn it on, and watch its runs
marvin platform workflows enable tag-new-posts
marvin platform workflows executions tag-new-posts

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
stdout carries data only; ✓ lines and dry-run summaries go to stderr.

# Ids of every disabled workflow
marvin platform workflows list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.enabled | not) | .id'

# Fail a deploy step if a workflow's latest run failed
status=$(marvin platform workflows executions tag-new-posts --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.[0].status')
[ "$status" = "success" ] || exit 1

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Command Endpoint list GET /api/automations get GET /api/automations/{id} options GET /api/automations/options create POST /api/automations update, enable, disable PATCH /api/automations/{id} delete DELETE /api/automations/{id} validate POST /api/automations/validate preview POST /api/automations/preview run POST /api/automations/{id}/run (?dry_run=true&entry_id=…&event_id=…) samples GET /api/automations/{id}/samples executions GET /api/automations/{id}/executions execution GET /api/automations/{id}/executions/{execution_id}

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Integrations — the providers that integration actions call, and their error policies
  • Event Log — event-log types lists the events a workflow can trigger on

docs.title: Workspace Members and Invites
docs.text: Who can work in a workspace: platform invites creates and revokes invitation links for new people, and platform workspace-members lists, adds, re-roles and removes people who already have a user account. Both are workspace-ADMIN tools. A SUPER_ADMIN managing memberships across workspaces uses marvin admin workspace-members, documented in admin-groups.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin platform invites list [--page <n>] [--per-page <n>] [--all]
marvin platform invites invite [--email <email>] [--uses <n>] [--role <role>]
marvin platform invites link --token <token>
marvin platform invites revoke --id <id> [--yes]

marvin platform workspace-members list <workspace-id>
marvin platform workspace-members get <workspace-id> <user-id>
marvin platform workspace-members add <workspace-id> (--user-id <id> --role <role> | --data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform workspace-members update-role <workspace-id> <user-id> (--role <role> | --data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin platform workspace-members remove <workspace-id> <user-id> --yes

Required role

Every command here, reads included, needs the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role. Without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: Invites
docs.text: An invitation is a token with a role and a number of uses. Its link lets a person join the workspace with that role.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
marvin platform invites list
marvin platform invites list --all --json
Option Description Default --page <number> Page number 1 --per-page <number> Items per page 50 --all Fetch every page (ignores --page) off

Columns: Token (first 20 characters), Role, Uses Left, Created. Table output ends with Total: <n> invitation token(s); with no invitations it prints No invitation tokens found.

docs.title: Invite
docs.text:
marvin platform invites invite --role AUTHOR
marvin platform invites invite --email ada@example.com --role EDITOR
marvin platform invites invite --uses 10 --role VIEWER

Creates an invitation token and prints its link; with --email it also emails the link.

Option Description Default --email <email> Send the invitation to this address (validated first) none (just print the link) --uses <number> Number of uses allowed 1 --role <role> Role for invited users: VIEWER, AUTHOR, EDITOR, ADMIN, OWNER EDITOR

In table mode the invitation URL is the only thing written to stdout, so URL=$(marvin platform invites invite) captures it; the token, role and remaining uses go to stderr. If the email cannot be sent the command says so and still prints the URL to share by hand. The token is shown in full only on a terminal; otherwise it is masked (first and last four characters) in the Token: line and in the JSON token field. The invitation URL always contains the full token, so treat it as a credential. With --json the output is {token, inviteUrl, usesLeft, workspaceRole}, or {token, inviteUrl, email, emailSent, error} when --email is given.

docs.title: Link
docs.text:
marvin platform invites link --token 5Xk2...

Prints the invitation URL for an existing token (--token <token>, required), as {"inviteUrl": ...} with --json. It builds the URL locally and does not check that the token is valid.

docs.title: Revoke
docs.text:
marvin platform invites revoke --id 0e6b94c2-1d73-4a58-9f20-b3c71a5d8e46 --yes
Option Description --id <id> Invitation token ID (required) --yes Skip confirmation

The link stops working. Without --yes the command asks Revoke this invitation? The link will stop working. (y/N) and cancels on anything but y. With --json it prints {"deleted": "<id>"}.

docs.title: Workspace members
docs.text: <workspace-id> is the workspace's UUID (marvin workspace list shows it) and <user-id> the user's UUID.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
marvin platform workspace-members list 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358
marvin platform workspace-members get 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358 c19d3f70-8a24-4e6b-b0d5-7f2e91a4c638

list columns: User ID, Username, Email, Role, Joined (date). get prints one member in full.

docs.title: Add
docs.text:
marvin platform workspace-members add 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358 --user-id c19d3f70-8a24-4e6b-b0d5-7f2e91a4c638 --role ADMIN
marvin platform workspace-members add 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358 --data '{"userId": "c19d3f70-8a24-4e6b-b0d5-7f2e91a4c638", "workspaceRole": "VIEWER"}'
Option Description --user-id <id> User ID to add --role <role> Workspace role: OWNER, ADMIN, EDITOR, AUTHOR or VIEWER (case-insensitive) --data <json\|@file\|-> Full body as inline JSON, @path, or - for stdin --file <path> Path to a JSON file (same as --data @path)

The flags form is used only when both --user-id and --role are given and there is no --data/--file; otherwise the body is read from --data, --file or piped stdin, with keys userId and workspaceRole (the older user_id / workspace_role spellings are still accepted). A role outside the five values above is rejected before anything is sent (Invalid role. Must be one of: OWNER, ADMIN, EDITOR, AUTHOR, VIEWER). Prints Added user to workspace with role: <role> on stderr and the member on stdout.

docs.title: Update role
docs.text:
marvin platform workspace-members update-role 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358 c19d3f70-8a24-4e6b-b0d5-7f2e91a4c638 --role VIEWER

Takes --role <role> (new role, same five values, case-insensitive) or a body via --data / --file / stdin ({"workspaceRole": "ADMIN"}); the same role check applies. Prints Updated member role to: <role> and the member.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
marvin platform workspace-members remove 5a8f0c3e-7d12-4b94-a6e1-92c4d0b7f358 c19d3f70-8a24-4e6b-b0d5-7f2e91a4c638 --yes

--yes is required (Remove requires --yes confirmation flag and exit 1 otherwise). With --json it prints {"deleted": "<user-id>"}. The user account itself is not deleted.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text: Switch between workspaces, store site tokens for the Publishing API, and export, back up, import and inspect the current workspace.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
marvin workspace current
marvin workspace use <workspace>
marvin workspace list
marvin workspace token [--for <slug>] [--from-stdin]
marvin workspace token:remove [--for <slug>]
marvin workspace export [-o, --out-file <file>] [--include-system-types] [--no-pretty]
marvin workspace import --file <path> [--overwrite]
marvin workspace preferences
marvin workspace preferences update (--data <json|@file|-> | --file <path>)
marvin workspace stats
marvin workspace backups list
marvin workspace backups create
marvin workspace backups download <filename> [-o, --out-file <file>]

All commands except current, token and token:remove call the Platform API and need a user token (marvin login, see Authentication); those three only read and write the local credentials file.

Required role

workspace export and workspace backups need the workspace ADMIN (or OWNER) role; without it the command fails with Permission denied (403) and names the role it needs. workspace import is restricted to a workspace OWNER (or a super admin) by the API. See Workspace roles.

docs.title: workspace current
docs.text:
Prints the active workspace slug from the local credentials; no network call. With --json / --yaml it prints {"slug": "<slug>"} (null when none is set).

marvin workspace current          # Active workspace: acme
marvin workspace current --json | jq -r '.slug'

docs.title: workspace use
docs.text:
Sets the active workspace by slug or ID, on the server session and in the local credentials. An unknown workspace prints the error and suggests marvin workspace list.

marvin workspace use acme

docs.title: workspace list
docs.text:
Lists the workspaces you can access. Table mode prints each as name (slug) with your role, an ACTIVE marker, the workspace ID, and a key symbol when a site token is stored for it. With --json you get an array of {workspace: {id, slug, name}, role, isActive}.

marvin workspace list
marvin workspace list --json | jq -r '.[].workspace.slug'

docs.title: workspace token
docs.text:
workspace token stores a site client token (for marvin publish ...) for a workspace. The token is not a command argument: you are prompted with hidden input, or pass --from-stdin to read it from a pipe. workspace token:remove deletes the stored token (and says so if none is stored).

Option Description Default --for <slug> Workspace slug Active workspace --from-stdin (token only) Read the token from stdin false 
marvin workspace token                                    # prompts
echo "$SITE_TOKEN" | marvin workspace token --from-stdin --for client-project
marvin workspace token:remove --for client-project

The stored token is used by marvin publish ahead of the MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN variable. You can also save one with marvin login --site-token <token> --workspace <slug>.

docs.title: workspace export
docs.text:
Exports the whole workspace as a JSON seed (content, structure, settings, integrations, workflows) for restore or migration. For a restorable ZIP use workspace backups create.

Option Description Default -o, --out-file <file> Write to a file instead of stdout stdout --include-system-types Include system entry types false --no-pretty Compact JSON instead of pretty-printed pretty 
marvin workspace export --out-file workspace.json
marvin workspace export --include-system-types --no-pretty > workspace.json

docs.title: workspace import
docs.text:
Imports a workspace bundle (a ZIP from workspace backups create / download).

Option Description Default --file <path> Path to the ZIP bundle (required) none --overwrite Overwrite existing records matched by slug false

Warning

--overwrite updates entries, collections, resources and assets that match by slug, and rebuilds their junction rows.

marvin workspace import --file backup.zip
marvin workspace import --file backup.zip --overwrite

It prints the number imported per record type.

docs.title: workspace preferences
docs.text:
marvin workspace preferences shows the current workspace's preferences. preferences update changes them from a JSON payload (--data inline, @file or - for stdin, or --file <path>); only the fields you send change, and the updated preferences are printed.

Fields include siteTitle, siteTagline, siteDescription, siteCanonicalUrl, siteLogo, siteFavicon, siteLocale, siteTimezone, siteContactEmail, siteAutoRebuild, siteSocialJson, siteMetadataJson, submissionProtectionJson, privateGroup, firstDayOfWeek and scheduledPublishRequiresApproval.

marvin workspace preferences
marvin workspace preferences update --data '{"siteTitle":"Acme","siteTimezone":"Europe/London"}'
marvin workspace preferences update --file prefs.json

docs.title: workspace stats
docs.text:
Shows platform-level counts for the current workspace (for example entries, assets, collections, webhooks, scheduled tasks, secrets, variables, members and AI usage).

marvin workspace stats
marvin workspace stats --json

docs.title: workspace backups
docs.text:
Server-side backups of the current workspace.

Command What it does backups list List available backups backups create Create a new backup and print the result backups download <filename> [-o, --out-file <file>] Download a backup by filename. Use --out-file for the ZIP; without it the data goes to stdout. 
marvin workspace backups create
