docs.title: Authentication Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for authenticating with the Marvin CLI.

docs.title: Authentication Methods
docs.text:
The Marvin CLI supports four authentication methods depending on which API you're using:

Method API Access Use Case Site Client Token Publishing API (read-only) Public content, frontend apps User Login Platform & Admin APIs Development, manual operations API Client Credentials Platform API Automation, CI/CD Admin Token Admin API System administration

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Site client tokens provide read-only access to the Publishing API for accessing published content.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
marvin_sk_<random_string>

Example: marvin_sk_1234567890abcdef

docs.title: Creating a Token
docs.text:
1. Log into Marvin
  2. Navigate to Settings → Publishing → Site Clients
  3. Click Create Site Client
  4. Enter a name and description
  5. Copy the generated token

Token Security

The token is only shown once. Store it securely. If lost, create a new token.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set in environment:

export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

Or in .env:

MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token

Or pass on command line:

marvin publish site --site-token marvin_sk_your_token

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Publishing API commands
marvin publish site
marvin publish entries
marvin publish collections

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Site client tokens have:

  • ✅ Read published entries
  • ✅ Read collections
  • ✅ Read assets
  • ✅ Read resources
  • ✅ Read site configuration
  • ❌ No access to drafts
  • ❌ No write operations
  • ❌ No platform/admin APIs

docs.title: Rotating Tokens
docs.text:
Best practice: Rotate tokens every 90 days.

# 1. Create new token in Marvin UI
# 2. Update environment
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_new_token
# 3. Test
marvin publish site
# 4. Delete old token in Marvin UI

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: User login provides full access to Platform and Admin APIs based on your user role.

docs.title: Interactive Login
docs.text:
marvin login

Prompts for a user token (hidden input). Create one in the Marvin UI or with marvin user tokens create.

docs.title: Non-Interactive Login
docs.text:
Using a command-line flag:

marvin login --user-token "$MARVIN_USER_TOKEN" --workspace my-workspace

Using an environment variable:

export MARVIN_USER_TOKEN=<your-user-token>
marvin login

Security Warning

Tokens passed on the command line end up in shell history. Prefer the interactive prompt or MARVIN_USER_TOKEN.

docs.title: Session Storage
docs.text:
After login, session tokens are stored securely:

  • macOS: Keychain (keychain-access)
  • Linux: Secret Service API (libsecret) or encrypted file
  • Windows: Credential Manager

Location (when file storage is used): 

~/.marvin/credentials

docs.title: Session Duration
docs.text: Sessions expire after: - 24 hours of inactivity - 7 days maximum - When explicitly logged out

docs.title: Checking Login Status
docs.text:
# Check if logged in
marvin user profile show

# In scripts
if marvin user profile show >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Logged in"
else
    echo "Not logged in"
fi

docs.title: Logging Out
docs.text:
marvin logout

Clears: - Session token - Cached user information - Stored credentials

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
User login permissions depend on workspace role:

Role Permissions VIEWER Read-only access AUTHOR Create/edit own entries EDITOR Manage all entries ADMIN Full workspace access OWNER Everything + billing

docs.title: Workspace Roles
docs.text:
Platform commands run as your user, and Marvin checks your role in the workspace before it acts. Roles rank OWNER > ADMIN > EDITOR > AUTHOR > VIEWER; a role can do everything the ones below it can.

Needs Commands ADMIN (or OWNER) platform webhooks (except types), platform incoming-webhooks, platform workflows, platform integrations (except providers), platform blueprints apply/update, platform variables, platform scheduled-tasks (except types), platform email-subscriptions, platform invites, platform workspace-members, platform api-clients, platform ai providers, platform email test-smtp/test-template/update-template, platform email-templates create/update/delete/test-send/event-connections, platform secrets create/update/delete/reveal, workspace export, workspace backups, events, platform entry-types create/update/delete, platform forms create/update/delete EDITOR platform collections create/update/delete/reorder/update-entry/order/preview, platform resources create/update/delete/apply-suggestion/reject-suggestion, platform assets update/delete/apply-suggestion/reject-suggestion, platform tags update/delete, tagging an asset or a resource, platform forms submissions, platform site, and changing anyone's entry or approving, publishing or scheduling one AUTHOR platform entries create (as a draft), changing or deleting your own entries until they are approved or published (including apply-suggestion/reject-suggestion, suggested-assets approve/reject and tagging them), platform tags create, platform assets upload VIEWER Reading: list and get on entries, collections, resources, assets, entry types, forms, tags and blueprints; entries counts, collections members, dashboard SUPER_ADMIN (platform role) Everything under marvin admin

Reads of workspace settings (webhooks, variables, scheduled tasks, API clients, members, backups) are ADMIN-only too, since they expose configuration.

When your role is too low the command exits with status 1 and says what it needs:

✗ Permission denied (403)
This needs the ADMIN role in workspace 'acme'.

Suggestions:
  • Ask a workspace OWNER or ADMIN to change your role (marvin platform workspace-members update-role)
  • Check you're in the right workspace: marvin workspace current

With --json the error is {"error": "...", "status": 403, "requiredRole": "ADMIN", "workspace": "acme"}. marvin <command> --help marks these commands with "(needs workspace ADMIN)" and the like.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: API clients provide programmatic access for automation without user credentials.

docs.title: Creating API Client
docs.text:
1. Log into Marvin
  2. Navigate to Settings → API → API Clients
  3. Click Create API Client
  4. Enter name and description
  5. Select permissions
  6. Copy client ID and secret

Secret Security

The secret is only shown once. Store it securely.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set in environment:

export MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
export MARVIN_API_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret

Or in .env:

MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
MARVIN_API_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When credentials are set, they're used automatically:

# No login needed
marvin platform entries
marvin platform entries create

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Configure granular permissions:

  • Read/write entries
  • Manage collections
  • Upload assets
  • Manage resources
  • Access webhooks
  • View event logs

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Create separate clients for different services
  2. Use minimal permissions for each client
  3. Rotate secrets every 90 days
  4. Monitor usage in event logs
  5. Revoke unused clients immediately

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Admin tokens provide system-level access for administrative operations.

docs.title: Creating Admin Token
docs.text:
1. Log into Marvin as admin
  2. Navigate to Admin → System → API Tokens
  3. Create new admin token
  4. Copy the token

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: export MARVIN_ADMIN_TOKEN=your_admin_token

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
marvin admin users
marvin admin system
marvin admin maintenance

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Admin tokens have full system access:

  • User management
  • System configuration
  • Maintenance operations
  • Cross-workspace access

Extreme Caution

Admin tokens have unrestricted access. Use sparingly and rotate frequently.

docs.title: Publishing API Flow
docs.text:
1. Get site client token from Marvin UI
2. Set MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN
3. Run publish commands

docs.title: Platform API Flow (User Login)
docs.text:
1. Run: marvin login
2. Enter email/password
3. Token stored in keychain
4. Run platform commands
5. Session expires or logout

docs.title: Platform API Flow (API Client)
docs.text:
1. Create API client in Marvin UI
2. Set MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID and MARVIN_API_CLIENT_SECRET
3. Run platform commands
4. Credentials used automatically

docs.title: Admin API Flow
docs.text:
1. Get admin token from Marvin UI
2. Set MARVIN_ADMIN_TOKEN
3. Run admin commands

docs.title: Token Management
docs.text:
1. Never commit credentials to version control
  2. Use secret managers in production (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, etc.)
  3. Rotate regularly - every 30-90 days
  4. Revoke immediately when compromised
  5. Monitor usage in audit logs

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
1. Principle of least privilege - minimum permissions needed
  2. Separate credentials per environment (dev, staging, prod)
  3. Different tokens for different services
  4. Audit regularly - review active tokens

docs.title: Development vs Production
docs.text:
Development: 

# User login is fine
marvin login

# Or site token in .env
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_dev_token

Production: 

# Use API client credentials
MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID=prod_client_id
MARVIN_API_CLIENT_SECRET=prod_client_secret

# Never use user credentials

docs.title: CI/CD Security
docs.text:
# GitHub Actions - use secrets
- name: Fetch Content
  env:
    MARVIN_API_URL: ${{ secrets.MARVIN_API_URL }}
    MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MARVIN_SITE_TOKEN }}
  run: marvin publish entries --json

Never: 

# DON'T DO THIS
- run: marvin publish site --site-token marvin_sk_hardcoded_token

docs.title: .env File Security
docs.text:
# Add to .gitignore
echo ".env" >> .gitignore
echo ".env.*" >> .gitignore
echo "!.env.example" >> .gitignore

# Set restrictive permissions
chmod 600 .env

docs.title: Invalid Token
docs.text:
Symptom: 401 Unauthorized

Solutions: 

# Check token is set
echo $MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN

# Verify token format
# Should start with marvin_sk_ for site tokens

# Create new token in Marvin UI
# Update environment
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_new_token

docs.title: Session Expired
docs.text:
Symptom: 401 Unauthorized after previous success

Solutions: 

# Log out and back in
marvin logout
marvin login

# Check session
marvin user profile show

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
Symptom: 403 Forbidden

Solutions: 

# Check user role
marvin user profile show --json | jq '.workspaceMemberships'

# Verify required permissions in Marvin UI
# Contact workspace admin if needed

docs.title: Token Storage Failed
docs.text:
Symptom: Cannot save credentials

Solutions: 

# Check directory permissions
ls -la ~/.marvin/

# Create directory if missing
mkdir -p ~/.marvin
chmod 700 ~/.marvin

# On macOS, grant keychain access if prompted

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Complete reference for all environment variables supported by the Marvin CLI.

docs.title: MARVIN_API_URL
docs.text:
Description: URL of your Marvin instance

Required: Yes

Format: Full URL with protocol

Examples: 

# Local development
MARVIN_API_URL=http://localhost:8000

# Docker
MARVIN_API_URL=http://marvin:8000

# Production
MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com

# Custom port
MARVIN_API_URL=https://marvin.example.com:3000

Default: None (must be set)

Override: --api-url <url>

docs.title: MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG
docs.text:
Description: Workspace slug to use

Required: Yes

Format: Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens

Examples: 

MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=my-workspace
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=production
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=acme-corp

Default: None (must be set)

Override: --workspace <slug>

docs.title: MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN
docs.text:
Description: Site client token for Publishing API

Required: For Publishing API commands

Format: marvin_sk_<random_string>

Example: 

MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_1234567890abcdef

Used by: - marvin publish * commands

Override: --site-token <token>

docs.title: MARVIN_EMAIL
docs.text:
Description: User email for authentication

Required: Optional (for non-interactive login)

Example: 

MARVIN_EMAIL=user@example.com

Used by: - marvin login (if not provided, prompts)

Security: Avoid in production, use API client instead

docs.title: MARVIN_PASSWORD
docs.text:
Description: User password for authentication

Required: Optional (for non-interactive login)

Example: 

MARVIN_PASSWORD=mypassword

Used by: - marvin login (if not provided, prompts)

Security: ⚠️ Never hardcode or commit to version control

docs.title: MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID
docs.text:
Description: API client ID for programmatic access

Required: For Platform API automation

Example: 

MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID=client_abc123

Used by: - marvin platform * commands (when set, no login needed)

docs.title: MARVIN_API_CLIENT_SECRET
docs.text:
Description: API client secret

Required: With MARVIN_API_CLIENT_ID

Example: 

MARVIN_API_CLIENT_SECRET=secret_xyz789

Used by: - marvin platform * commands

Security: Store securely, rotate regularly

docs.title: MARVIN_ADMIN_TOKEN
docs.text:
Description: Admin token for system operations

Required: For Admin API commands

Example: 

MARVIN_ADMIN_TOKEN=admin_token_123

Used by: - marvin admin * commands

Security: ⚠️ Extreme caution - full system access

docs.title: MARVIN_OUTPUT_FORMAT
docs.text:
Description: Default output format

Required: No

Values: table, json, yaml, csv

Example: 

MARVIN_OUTPUT_FORMAT=json

Default: table

Override: --output <format>, --json, --yaml, --csv (a flag always wins over the variable)

docs.title: MARVIN_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Description: Request timeout in milliseconds

Required: No

Format: Integer (milliseconds)

Example: 

MARVIN_TIMEOUT=30000  # 30 seconds

Default: 30000 (30 seconds)

Override: --timeout <ms>

docs.title: MARVIN_INSECURE
docs.text:
Description: Disable SSL certificate verification

Required: No

Values: true, false

Example: 

MARVIN_INSECURE=true  # Development only!

Default: false

Security: ⚠️ Never use in production

docs.title: MARVIN_DEBUG
docs.text:
Description: Enable debug logging

Required: No

Values: true, false

Example: 

MARVIN_DEBUG=true

Default: false

Output includes: - HTTP requests/responses - Authentication flow - API endpoints - Response times

docs.title: DEBUG
docs.text:
Description: Enable detailed debug output (npm debug module)

Required: No

Values: Namespace pattern

Examples: 

# All marvin debug output
DEBUG=marvin:*

# Specific modules
DEBUG=marvin:api,marvin:auth

# All debug output
DEBUG=*

docs.title: .env File
docs.text:
Load variables from a .env file:

# .env
MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=production
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_token
MARVIN_OUTPUT_FORMAT=json

The CLI automatically loads .env from the current directory.

docs.title: Multiple .env Files
docs.text:
Use different files for different environments:

# .env.development
MARVIN_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=dev

# .env.staging
MARVIN_API_URL=https://staging.example.com
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=staging

# .env.production
MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=production

Load specific file:

# Using dotenv-cli
dotenv -e .env.staging -- marvin publish entries

# Or manually
export $(cat .env.staging | grep -v '^#' | xargs)
marvin publish entries

docs.title: Variable Priority
docs.text:
Variables are resolved in this order (highest priority first):

  1. Command-line flags - --api-url, --workspace, etc.
  2. Environment variables - Exported in shell
  3. .env file - In current directory
  4. Default values - Built-in defaults

Example:

# .env file
MARVIN_API_URL=http://localhost:8000

# Environment variable (overrides .env)
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://staging.example.com

# Command-line flag (overrides everything)
marvin --api-url https://api.example.com publish entries
# Uses: https://api.example.com

docs.title: Shell Export
docs.text:
# Single session
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_token

# Verify
echo $MARVIN_API_URL

docs.title: Shell Profile
docs.text:
Add to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, or ~/.profile:

# Marvin CLI configuration
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
export MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=my-workspace
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_token

Reload:

source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Per-Command
docs.text:
# Inline environment
MARVIN_OUTPUT_FORMAT=json marvin publish entries

# Multiple variables
MARVIN_API_URL=https://staging.example.com \
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=staging \
marvin publish entries

docs.title: 1. Never Commit Credentials
docs.text:
# .gitignore
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

docs.title: 2. Use .env.example
docs.text:
Create a template without secrets:

# .env.example
MARVIN_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=your-workspace-slug
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_your_token_here

docs.title: 3. Restrict File Permissions

docs.title: 4. Use Secret Managers in Production
docs.text:
# AWS Secrets Manager
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
  --secret-id marvin/site-token \
  --query SecretString \
  --output text)

# HashiCorp Vault
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=$(vault kv get -field=token secret/marvin)

docs.title: 5. Separate Credentials per Environment
docs.text:
# Development
.env.development

# Staging
.env.staging

# Production
.env.production (use secret manager instead)

docs.title: Variable Not Set
docs.text:
Symptom: "MARVIN_API_URL is required"

Solution: 

# Check variable
echo $MARVIN_API_URL

# Set variable
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com

# Or create .env file
cat > .env << EOF
MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=my-workspace
EOF

docs.title: Variable Not Loaded from .env
docs.text:
Symptom: CLI doesn't use .env values

Solution:

# Check .env format (no spaces around =)
cat .env

# Reload if using dotenv-cli
dotenv -- marvin publish entries

docs.title: Wrong Environment

Solution:

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Guide to handling errors and troubleshooting issues with the Marvin CLI.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
The CLI uses standard exit codes to indicate success or failure:

Code Category Meaning 0 Success Command completed successfully 1 General Error Generic error (see error message) 400 Bad Request Invalid request parameters 401 Unauthorized Authentication failed 403 Forbidden Permission denied 404 Not Found Resource doesn't exist 429 Too Many Requests Rate limit exceeded 500 Server Error Internal server error 503 Service Unavailable Server is down or overloaded

docs.title: Using Exit Codes
docs.text:
# Check if command succeeded
if marvin publish entry homepage --json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Entry exists"
    exit 0
else
    echo "Entry not found"
    exit 1
fi

# Capture exit code
marvin publish entries --json
EXIT_CODE=$?

if [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Failed with code: $EXIT_CODE"
    case $EXIT_CODE in
        401) echo "Authentication failed" ;;
        404) echo "Resource not found" ;;
        500) echo "Server error" ;;
        *) echo "Unknown error" ;;
    esac
    exit $EXIT_CODE
fi

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: 401 Unauthorized
Authentication failed

Causes: - Invalid site client token - Expired user session - Missing credentials

Solutions:

For Publishing API: 

# Check token is set
echo $MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN

# Verify token format (should start with marvin_sk_)
# Generate new token in Marvin UI if needed
export MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_new_token

For Platform API: 

# Log out and log back in
marvin logout
marvin login

# Verify authentication
marvin user profile show

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
Symptom: 

✗ Permission denied (403)
This needs the ADMIN role in workspace 'acme'.

Causes: - Your role in the workspace is below what the command needs (settings commands need ADMIN, content changes EDITOR, entry types and forms ADMIN; see Workspace roles) - You're in a different workspace than you meant - marvin admin commands need the SUPER_ADMIN platform role

Solutions: 

# Which workspace am I in?
marvin workspace current

# Ask a workspace OWNER or ADMIN to change your role, e.g.
marvin platform workspace-members update-role --help

docs.title: Cannot Connect to API
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: connect ECONNREFUSED
Cannot connect to Marvin API

Causes: - Wrong API URL - Server is down - Network issue - Firewall blocking connection

Solutions: 

# Verify API URL
echo $MARVIN_API_URL

# Test connectivity
curl $MARVIN_API_URL/health

# Check server is running
# For local development:
cd /path/to/marvin
python -m uvicorn marvin.main:app --reload

# Check firewall/VPN settings

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: Request timeout
Operation took too long

Causes: - Slow network - Large dataset - Server overloaded

Solutions: 

# Increase timeout
export MARVIN_TIMEOUT=60000  # 60 seconds
marvin publish entries

# Or per command
marvin --timeout 60000 publish entries

# Limit results to reduce load
marvin publish entries --limit 100

# Check server performance

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: 404 Not Found
Resource does not exist

Causes: - Entry/collection/resource doesn't exist - Wrong slug - Wrong workspace - Entry not published (for Publishing API)

Solutions: 

# Verify workspace
echo $MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG
marvin workspace list

# Check slug spelling
marvin publish entries --json | jq -r '.[].slug'

# For Publishing API, check entry is published
marvin platform entries --json | jq '.[] | select(.slug == "homepage")'

# Verify it exists
marvin publish collections  # List all collections
marvin publish entries         # List all entries

docs.title: Missing Required Variable
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: MARVIN_API_URL is required
Please set MARVIN_API_URL environment variable

Causes: - Environment variable not set - .env file missing or not loaded

Solutions: 

# Check environment
env | grep MARVIN

# Set variables
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
export MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=my-workspace

# Create .env file
cat > .env << EOF
MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com
MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG=my-workspace
MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN=marvin_sk_token
EOF

# Verify .env exists
ls -la .env

docs.title: Invalid Configuration
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: Invalid API URL format
URL must include protocol (http:// or https://)

Solutions: 

# Check URL format
echo $MARVIN_API_URL

# Correct format
export MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com  # Good
# Not:
# export MARVIN_API_URL=api.example.com  # Missing protocol
# export MARVIN_API_URL=https://api.example.com/  # Trailing slash

docs.title: Invalid JSON
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: Unexpected token in JSON at position 0

Causes: - Server returned HTML instead of JSON - Malformed JSON response - Wrong endpoint

Solutions: 

# Check API URL is correct
curl $MARVIN_API_URL/health

# Verify endpoint
# Use table output to see raw response
marvin publish entries

# Enable debug mode
export MARVIN_DEBUG=true
marvin publish entries --json

docs.title: Empty Response
docs.text:
Symptom: 

Error: No data returned

Causes: - No published content - Filters too restrictive - Wrong workspace

Solutions: 

# Check without filters
marvin publish entries

# Verify workspace has content
marvin --workspace correct-slug publish entries

# List available content
marvin publish collections
marvin publish entries

docs.title: Retry Logic
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

MAX_RETRIES=3
RETRY_DELAY=5

for i in $(seq 1 $MAX_RETRIES); do
    if marvin publish entries --json > entries.json; then
        echo "Success on attempt $i"
        exit 0
    else
        EXIT_CODE=$?
        echo "Attempt $i failed with code $EXIT_CODE"

        if [ $i -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; then
            echo "Retrying in $RETRY_DELAY seconds..."
            sleep $RETRY_DELAY
        fi
    fi
done

echo "Failed after $MAX_RETRIES attempts"
exit 1

docs.title: Exponential Backoff
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

MAX_RETRIES=5
DELAY=1

for i in $(seq 1 $MAX_RETRIES); do
    if marvin publish entries --json; then
        exit 0
    else
        if [ $i -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; then
            echo "Retry $i in ${DELAY}s..."
            sleep $DELAY
            DELAY=$((DELAY * 2))  # Exponential backoff
        fi
    fi
done

exit 1

docs.title: Graceful Degradation
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

# Try to get entries, fall back to cached version
if marvin publish entries --json > entries.json 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Fetched fresh data"
else
    echo "Using cached data"
    if [ ! -f entries-cache.json ]; then
        echo "Error: No cache available"
        exit 1
    fi
    cp entries-cache.json entries.json
fi

# Always cache successful fetches
if [ -f entries.json ]; then
    cp entries.json entries-cache.json
fi

export MARVIN_DEBUG=true
marvin publish entries

# Debug module (more detailed)
DEBUG=marvin:* marvin publish entries

# Specific modules
DEBUG=marvin:api,marvin:auth marvin publish entries

docs.title: Inspect Requests
docs.text:

MARVIN_DEBUG=true marvin publish entries 2>&1 | tee debug.log

# Review debug log
less debug.log

docs.title: Check API Directly
docs.text:
# Test API endpoint
API_URL=$MARVIN_API_URL
WORKSPACE=$MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG
TOKEN=$MARVIN_SITE_CLIENT_TOKEN

docs.title: Log to File
docs.text:
# Log output
marvin publish entries > output.log 2>&1

# Log errors only
marvin publish entries 2> errors.log

# Log with timestamp
marvin publish entries 2>&1 | while read line; do
    echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') $line"

docs.title: Structured Logging
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

LOG_FILE="marvin.log"

log() {
    local level=$1
    shift
    echo "$(date -Iseconds) [$level] $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

log INFO "Starting entry fetch"

if marvin publish entries --json > entries.json 2>/dev/null; then
    log INFO "Successfully fetched entries"
else
    log ERROR "Failed to fetch entries (exit code: $?)"
    exit 1
fi

docs.title: Capture Error Details
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

COMMAND="marvin publish entries --json"
OUTPUT=$(mktemp)
ERRORS=$(mktemp)

# Run command and capture output/errors
$COMMAND > "$OUTPUT" 2> "$ERRORS"
EXIT_CODE=$?

if [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]; then
    cat <<EOF
Command failed: $COMMAND
Exit code: $EXIT_CODE
Time: $(date)
Environment:
  API_URL: $MARVIN_API_URL
  WORKSPACE: $MARVIN_WORKSPACE_SLUG

Error output:
$(cat "$ERRORS")

Debug info:
$(marvin --version)
$(env | grep MARVIN)
EOF
fi

rm "$OUTPUT" "$ERRORS"
exit $EXIT_CODE

docs.title: Send Error Notifications
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

if ! marvin publish entries --json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Send email alert
    echo "Marvin CLI failed at $(date)" | \
        mail -s "Marvin CLI Error" admin@example.com

    # Or send Slack notification
    curl -X POST https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/URL \
         -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{
           "text": "Marvin CLI error in production",
           "attachments": [{
             "color": "danger",
             "fields": [{
               "title": "Environment",
               "value": "Production"
             }]
           }]
         }'
fi

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always check exit codes in scripts
  2. Use timeout for long-running commands
  3. Implement retry logic for transient failures
  4. Log errors with context
  5. Validate configuration before running commands
  6. Cache successful responses for fallback
  7. Monitor error rates in production
  8. Set up alerting for critical failures
